Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at0 and infinity; the integral affine chart coordinate rings are Z[q] and Z[q^-1].

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ ($\lambda\in P^+$). Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$ (well defined because the highest vector is fixed). Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]; $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)$ are $\psi$-stable). Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$. The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction, whereas E is a Z-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice M_A. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. Intersections M_A∩L and M_A∩L^- are respectively Z[q]- and Z[q^-1]-modules, generally not A-modules. The balanced part E is a Z-module; its Laurent extension A⊗_Z E is the full integral module once globalization is proved. More generally a based integrable module (M,B) here means exactly: B is a homogeneous field basis; M_A=⊕_b A b is U_A-stable; the semilinear involution fixing B is U/bar compatible; and L0=⊕_b A0 b with residue B is a crystal local basis at0. These are Lusztig27.1.2(a)–(d) after v=q^-1 and the integrable Bao–Wang extension. Such data do not automatically imply integral Θ action on an arbitrary based pair. A based subobject is a U-submodule spanned by a subset of B; a based quotient is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send B to the target basis or0 and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral/bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.
scaffold.strategy: A definition fixing the three lattices. The involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ maps $A_0$ isomorphically onto $A_\infty$, so $\psi(L)$ is an $A_\infty$-lattice generating $M$. $\psi(M_A)=M_A$ holds on $U_A$ by [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]], and $V_A(\lambda)$ is $\psi$-stable because $\psi(F_{i_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{i_k}^{(r_k)}v_\lambda)=F_{i_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{i_k}^{(r_k)}v_\lambda$ on divided-power monomials. Nothing is asserted about $M_A\cap L$; in particular the definition hides no integral-freeness assumption and no self-duality of the lower lattice. No choice principle is used. The general four based conditions are checked independently; the associated bar fixes a field basis but U compatibility and U_A stability are real requirements. Basis-subset subobjects give saturated free integral sublattices and free complementary quotients. Their bars are the restrictions/quotients of the ambient bar, and their crystal local data are inherited because their subset/kernel is closed under the module action and the residue operators. This is the actual source27.1.3–27.1.4 interface, not an assumed integral splitting of a semisimple field module.

The example computes the dual crystal of [[prop-dual-crystal-and-reversal-conventions]] in two small cases.

(A) For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$, let $B(1)=\{v_0\xrightarrow{1}v_1\}$ with $wt(v_0)=\lambda_1,\ wt(v_1)=-\lambda_1$ and $\varepsilon_1(v_0)=0,\varphi_1(v_0)=1,\varepsilon_1(v_1)=1,\varphi_1(v_1)=0$ (as in [[ex-tensor-crystal-b-one-tensor-b-one-for-sl-two]]). Then $B(1)^\vee=\{v_0^\vee,v_1^\vee\}$ has the single arrow $v_1^\vee\xrightarrow{1}v_0^\vee$, weights $wt(v_0^\vee)=-\lambda_1,\ wt(v_1^\vee)=\lambda_1$, and $(\varepsilon_1,\varphi_1)$ equal to $(1,0)$ at $v_0^\vee$ and $(0,1)$ at $v_1^\vee$. Hence $B(1)^\vee\cong B(1)$ as crystals, realized with the highest vertex $v_1^\vee$.

(B) For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3$, let $B(\lambda_1)=\{u_1\xrightarrow{1}u_2\xrightarrow{2}u_3\}$ be the standard crystal of [[ex-highest-components-in-a-small-type-a-two-tensor-crystal]]. (C) On the tensor square of (A), $(B(1)\otimes B(1))^\vee\cong B(1)^\vee\otimes B(1)^\vee$ under $(b_1\otimes b_2)^\vee\mapsto b_2^\vee\otimes b_1^\vee$; both sides split as $B(2)\sqcup B(0)$ because each of $B(2),B(0)$ is self-dual along the chain reversal (weights $2\lambda_1,0,-2\lambda_1$ are symmetric).

scaffold.strategy:
## Right strings and the adapted survivor criterion, initially with signs

Define the right string operators by star conjugating the left normalized Kashiwara operators. Because star is an isometry of the actual crystal lattice and signed crystal set, every positive crystal residue b lies in exactly one right-string position c_i(b)>=0. On a lattice lift u one has

    u=sum_(n>=0) u_n F_i^(n),   u_n in ker(star e_i' star),

with every u_n in the crystal lattice, and modulo q only the component n=c_i(b) is nonzero. Its top coefficient has residue ±bar b for some positive crystal residue bar b with c_i(bar b)=0. For the negative half the lattice-component argument is proved directly by the same finite tail calculation as the module string lemma: if u=sum_n F_i^(n)v_n, set T_n=e-tilde_i^n u; then v_n=T_n-f-tilde_i T_(n+1) lies in the lattice. Induction on the largest position, using the residue partial inverse, shows that a basis residue has exactly one nonzero component and that its top residue is positive. Root height makes the tails finite. This proves the half version without applying an integrable-module-only Statement to U^-. Conjugating this argument through the signed lattice theorem gives the asserted signed right version, without assuming unsigned star. The integer c_i(b) is epsilon_i of the absolute value of star b.

The field right ideal U^- F_i^t is the direct sum of right-string positions n>=t. Its adapted global subset is therefore precisely the positive indices b with c_i(b)>=t: conjugate the already proved left-string adapted global subset through star, whose possible signs do not affect which A-basis vectors span the ideal. The based quotient's field kernel is the sum of these right ideals at t=lambda_i+1. Since all are adapted to ONE global basis, their sum is the span of the union of their basis subsets. Therefore

    pi_lambda(b)!=0 iff c_i(b)<=lambda_i for every i.    (A)

This proves the highest-weight survivor criterion already with signed star. It neither assumes unsigned star nor infers an adapted intersection from an arbitrary linear sum. The surviving residues are bijective with B(lambda) by the existing based quotient/grand loop. Raising cannot turn a survivor into a killed nonzero residue: if e_i b were killed, the ALL-residue lowering identity pi_lambda(f_i(e_i b))=f_i pi_lambda(e_i b)=0 and the negative-half partial inverse f_i e_i b=b would force b killed, a contradiction. Thus every nonzero raising iterate of a survivor survives. Combining this with the surviving-residue raising identity proves equality of the entire raising lengths, epsilon_i(pi_lambda b)=epsilon_i(b), including the zero endpoint. This supplies the precise statistic identification used later in the finite-model construction without circularly using elementary embeddings. Raising on survivors and surviving lowering are exactly these existing projection compatibilities. The shifted statistics are epsilon_i(b) and epsilon_i(b)+<h_i,lambda+wt(b)> because B(lambda) is the actual highest-weight module crystal; raising preservation gives epsilon equality, and its rank-one formula gives phi.

## Canonical elementary embedding by finite highest-weight tensor models

Fix color i and a finite set of lowering words of height at most H. Work in the regularized finite support. Choose lambda_i=0 and lambda_j large for j!=i, large enough that no right ideal for those j meets any relevant root component of height at most H+1. Choose N>H+1. The total label lambda+N Lambda_i is then large at every relevant color, so its projection identifies the canonical B(infinity) vertices and all edges under consideration with the corresponding finite-degree vertices of B(lambda+N Lambda_i). Apply the strict highest-weight tensor embedding into B(lambda) tensor B(N Lambda_i).

Throughout these finite lowering paths the second factor is a pure i-string f_i^m u_(N Lambda_i). Indeed initially it is highest. For j!=i its epsilon_j is0 at every pure i-string position: E_j commutes with F_i and kills the highest vector, so all such vectors are E_j-highest. The first factor's phi_j is positive and larger than any second epsilon_j in the bounded degree, because lambda_j is chosen large. Thus both lowering and raising of any j!=i act on the first factor. Color i preserves the pure i-string form. Its string endpoint N is not reached in this height bound.

Lift the first residue b_1 uniquely to its surviving positive residue b' in B(infinity). Replace the second pure i-position m by b_i(-m) in the elementary crystal. The finite tensor rules become exactly those on B(infinity) tensor B_i: for i, lambda_i=0 means the first phi_i is epsilon_i(b')+<h_i,wt(b')>, and the second epsilon_i is m. For j!=i the elementary statistics are -infinity, so its tensor rule selects the first factor, just as the large-lambda finite model does. The finite tensor epsilon formula reduces to epsilon_j(b') for j!=i because lambda_j is large; for i it reduces to max(epsilon_i(b'),m-<h_i,wt(b')>). Root weights add to wt(b')-m alpha_i. Thus the replacement preserves the generic weight, epsilon and formal phi statistics as well as every considered operator.

This construction is independent of lambda,N WITHOUT assuming a stabilization theorem. Define its candidate value on a lowering word w by computing w(u_infinity tensor b_i(0)) using the actual generic tensor rules. The preceding finite-model argument shows that this computation agrees with the replacement of the finite tensor image for every bounded path. If two words w,w' give the same b in B(infinity), choose one common finite bound and one common pair lambda,N. Their images in B(lambda+N Lambda_i) coincide, hence their strict tensor images coincide, and the unique surviving lifts of their first factors coincide. Therefore the candidate generic tensor values coincide. Conversely if the candidate values coincide, choose the same finite model for the two words; its first-factor projections and second positions coincide, and injectivity of Phi followed by the large-label projection identification gives w u_infinity=w' u_infinity. This proves a well-defined injective Psi_i, independent of all choices.

For lowering use the same finite model on a word and that word with one appended operator. For raising use a model containing the vertex, its raising neighbor if nonzero, and the next boundary; strictness of finite Phi and the already checked branch/statistic formulas give Psi_i(e_j b)=e_j Psi_i(b), including zero. Hence

    Psi_i:B(infinity)->B(infinity) tensor B_i

is strict, sends the vacuum to u_infinity tensor b_i(0), and every elementary coordinate is nonpositive. This is an actual finite-word construction, rather than a citation to Kashiwara Theorem8.2.

## Identifying the elementary coordinate with the right-string index

## Identification of the generic and cyclotomic module crystals

the preceding local one-step and jump/embedding lemmas construct the generic module strict elementary embeddings, with extraction coordinate epsilon_i^L and positive extraction on every nonvacuum module. Both its graph and the canonical graph just constructed are generated by lowering words from their vacua and have every lowering operator nonzero.     epsilon_i^L(M)=epsilon_i^star(b_M).

## Finite-extraction comparison proof

There is a smaller recognition contract for this application, whose proof is elementary. Suppose C and D are crystals, each generated from its unique weight-zero vertex by lowering words, every f_i is everywhere nonzero, and each has strict elementary embeddings Psi_i with nonpositive elementary coordinates and a positive coordinate for some i on every nonvacuum vertex. Assume the weight support of a vertex is finite and extraction subtracts a nonnegative multiple of alpha_i from its root weight. Then there is a unique crystal isomorphism C=D carrying the two vacua to each other.

Proof. Fix a finite color set containing the support of a lowering word. Cycle through these colors, applying Psi_i to the current first factor, and leave every elementary tensor factor already extracted in place. Tensoring a strict embedding with identity maps is strict: for each color the tensor max formulas preserve epsilon/phi and weight, hence preserve the branch inequality including equality. Therefore every finite composite is strict and injective. Each extraction lowers the nonnegative height of the first factor by its elementary coordinate c. If an entire cycle makes no extraction from a nonvacuum factor, that factor is unchanged throughout the cycle, yet its support has a color with positive extraction, contradiction. Thus after at most the starting height many cycles (and one harmless final cycle) the first factor is the vacuum. Extraction of absent colors is zero: a nonzero alpha_i extraction would give a residual root weight with negative alpha_i coefficient, forbidden. Consequently this finite procedure works in both crystals using the same finite color cycle.

For a word w of length h, use h+1 cycles. Every prefix has height at most h, so both images of every prefix have vacuum first factor. Strictness computes the image of w by applying that same lowering word to the same tensor of a vacuum and elementary zero vertices. While the underlying vacua belong to different crystals, their weights and epsilon/phi are identical and their raising operators vanish; at each intermediate prefix the first factor is still the vacuum, so a nonzero lowering operation cannot take place in that first factor. All operations occur in the identical elementary factors, and the resulting elementary coordinates are identical. If two words w,w' produce the same vertex in C, use a common finite color set and enough cycles for both lengths; their identical C images give identical coordinate tensors, hence identical D images and, by injectivity, identical D vertices. Interchanging C and D gives the converse. Mapping a lowering word in C to that word in D is therefore a well-defined bijection. It preserves lowering by construction, raising by partial inverses, weights by word content, and epsilon/phi because the common strict finite tensor embeddings preserve these statistics. Uniqueness follows from lowering generation. This proves the lemma.

Then for every i,n≥1 the image string-ideal J_(i,n)^A in each highest module, with its rational zero/infinity chart intersections, is integrally balanced in degree lambda−alpha. Its balanced Z-intersection maps isomorphically to the Z-span of Bλ∩f̃_i^n Bλ in that degree. Similarly the half ideal I_(i,n)^A is integrally balanced in degree−alpha, with residue Z-span B∞∩f̃_i^n B∞. Their Laurent extensions are free A-modules with these adapted global lifts. If n+mu(h_i)<0, the boundary generation identity of the preceding supplier gives J_(i,−mu(h_i))^A_mu=V_A_mu, hence J_(i,n)^A_mu is the same full component as the already handled larger-n ideal. By definition J_n=F_i^(n)V_A[mu+n alpha_i]+J_(n+1). The lower-degree based quotient expresses the source V_A component using lower G∞(b) with surviving pi_lambda(b). If ẽ_i b≠0, lower-height negative-half string membership puts G∞(b) in I_(i,1)^A, so F_i^(n)G∞(b) lies in I_(i,n+1)^A by multiplying divided powers (integer Gaussians). It contributes only to J_(n+1). The remaining finite Z-module F is generated by phi_b=F_i^(n)G∞(b)v_lambda for ẽ_i b=0 and surviving image; their lower degree global lifts are bar fixed. To see phi_b∈L_mu+J_(n+1), extract P_iG∞(b): G∞(b)−P_iG∞(b) lies in F_iU^- with integral string coefficients, so its F_i^(n) multiple is in the image J_(n+1). The condition n+mu(h_i)≥0 ensures the module string at the surviving top class has length at least n; thus f̃_i^n pi(b) is nonzero and at exactly positionn. scaffold.statement:
Let $M_1,M_2$ be chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ carry the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure of [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]] given by the coproduct $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, $\Delta K_h=K_h\otimes K_h$ of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Then:

(a) **Grading.** $M_1\otimes M_2$ is a chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module for $(M_1\otimes M_2)_\mu=\bigoplus_{\mu_1+\mu_2=\mu}(M_1)_{\mu_1}\otimes(M_2)_{\mu_2}$, a direct sum by [[thm-tensor-products-commute-with-arbitrary-direct-sums]].

(b) **Integrability.** If $M_1,M_2$ are integrable then so is $M_1\otimes M_2$: $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every pure tensor, hence on the whole module.

(c) **Finite weights and bounded support.** If in addition every label-weight space of $M_1,M_2$ is finite dimensional and each weight set is contained in a finite union of cones $\lambda-Q_+$, then the same holds for $M_1\otimes M_2$.

(d) **Tensored lattices.** If $(L_1,B_1),(L_2,B_2)$ are crystal bases of $M_1,M_2$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), then $L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2$ is a free $A_0$-submodule of $M_1\otimes M_2$ generating it over $\mathbb Q(q)$, satisfies $(L_1\otimes L_2)_\mu=\bigoplus_{\mu_1+\mu_2=\mu}(L_1)_{\mu_1}\otimes(L_2)_{\mu_2}$, and $B_1\otimes B_2$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $(L_1\otimes L_2)/q(L_1\otimes L_2)$ compatible with these weight decompositions.

No choice principle is used.
scaffold.strategy:
(a) $\Delta K_h$ acts on $(M_1)_{\mu_1}\otimes(M_2)_{\mu_2}$ by $q^{\langle\mu_1,h\rangle}q^{\langle\mu_2,h\rangle}=q^{\langle\mu_1+\mu_2,h\rangle}$, and $\Delta E_i$, $\Delta F_i$ shift the bidegree by $\alpha_i$ and $-\alpha_i$; the direct sum over bidegrees is the published compatibility of tensor products with direct sums.

(b) Put $x:=F_i\otimes1$ and $y:=K_i\otimes F_i$; then $yx=q_i^{-2}xy$, so [[lem-q-binomial-expansion-for-q-commuting-elements]] gives $\Delta(F_i)^n=(x+y)^n=\sum_{j=0}^n\gamma_{n,j}F_i^{\,n-j}K_i^{\,j}\otimes F_i^{\,j}$ with $\gamma_{n,j}\in\mathbb Q(q)$ (only finiteness of the sum matters). On $u\otimes v$ choose $A$ with $F_i^Au=F_i^Av=0$; every term with $n>2A$ has $n-j>A$ or $j>A$ and vanishes, so $F_i$ is locally nilpotent on $u\otimes v$. The same argument with $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, using $(1\otimes E_i)(E_i\otimes K_i^{-1})=q_i^{2}(E_i\otimes K_i^{-1})(1\otimes E_i)$, gives local nilpotence of $E_i$; local nilpotence on all pure tensors gives it on every vector.

(c) For fixed $\mu$ the space $(M_1\otimes M_2)_\mu$ is the sum over pairs $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$ with $\mu_1+\mu_2=\mu$ and both label spaces nonzero. Writing $\mu_j=\lambda_j-\nu_j$ with $\nu_j\in Q_+$ inside the finitely many cones containing the weight sets, the relation $\nu_1+\nu_2=\lambda_1+\lambda_2-\mu$ has only finitely many solutions, so the sum is finite and each term is finite dimensional. The weight set of $M_1\otimes M_2$ is contained in the sum of the finitely many cones.

(d) $L_1\otimes L_2$ is free, and $\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}(L_1\otimes L_2)\cong M_1\otimes M_2$ by the generation hypotheses; the weight decomposition is the tensor product of the direct sum decompositions of $L_1$ and $L_2$. Since $q(L_1\otimes L_2)=qL_1\otimes L_2+L_1\otimes qL_2$, right exactness of the tensor product gives $(L_1\otimes L_2)/q(L_1\otimes L_2)\cong(L_1/qL_1)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}(L_2/qL_2)$, so $B_1\otimes B_2$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis, weight-graded. Only the easy lattice conditions are established here; stability under the crystal operators is the tensor product theorem on this page.

scaffold.statement:
Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'\iff b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite epsilon_i on each element, formal phi_i=epsilon_i+<h_i,wt>, and actual lowering length ell_i^-=infinity. Every f̃_i iterate is nonzero because ẽ_i f̃_i=id holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph Definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.
scaffold.strategy:
All content is read off from the grand loop, exactly as in Kashiwara's Theorem 4 and JKK Theorem 7.1(b).

(i) $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is by definition the $A_0$-span of the monomials $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$; each weight piece is a finitely generated $A_0$-module ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]](c)) inside the finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q(q)$-space $U_q^-[-\alpha]$, hence torsion-free and free over the principal ideal domain $A_0$ ([[cor-finitely-generated-torsion-free-modules-over-a-pid-are-free]]); this gives the freeness in (i) and the decomposition in (ii), and $\mathcal L(\infty)\otimes_{A_0}\mathbb Q(q)=U_q^-$ by the argument of Step 7 of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]] (for $\lambda\gg0$ the map $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-[-\alpha]\to V(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is an isomorphism and $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$). Stability of $\mathcal L(\infty)$ under $\tilde f_i$ is by construction (a $\tilde f$-monomial is a monomial), and stability under $\tilde e_i$ is clause H(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]](i). The basis statement and $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ are clauses K(r) and I(r); $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$ because a $\tilde f_i$-image of a monomial is a monomial and because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}$ prevents the class from vanishing modulo $q$; and the partial-inverse axiom follows from clause J(r) together with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}$: if $\tilde f_ib=b'$ then $b=\tilde e_ib'$ by [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii), and conversely if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ with $b'=\tilde f_ib''$ then $b=b''$ by J(r), so $b'=\tilde f_ib$. The rank formula in (ii) is K(r) together with the spanning of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ over $A_0$ and the equality $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\otimes_{A_0}\mathbb Q(q)=U_q^-[-\alpha]$.

(iii) is the content of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]], which is proved from the same induction; the surjectivity of $\pi_\lambda$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is its clause (c).

(iv) $\tilde f_i$ is injective on $U_q^-$ by [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii), so $\varphi_i(b)=\infty$ for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)$, while $\varepsilon_i(b)<\infty$ by the definition of the crystal basis; the remaining properties of [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]] are parts of the crystal-basis axioms. The axiom of choice is inherited through clause J(r) of the grand loop, which the partial-inverse axiom uses via [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] (JKK Proposition 7.29); it is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Apart from that inheritance, all lattices involved are finitely generated over the principal ideal domain $A_0$ and no choice is used. Interpret formal phi_i by the corrected negative-half convention; it is not the number of remaining lowering arrows. The ẽ_i f̃_i identity proves nonvanishing directly modulo q, not merely by field injectivity.

(a) **Highest vertices.** For $b=b_1\otimes b_2\in B_1\otimes B_2$ the following are equivalent: (i) $b$ is a highest weight element, i.e. $\tilde e_ib=0$ for every $i\in I$; (ii) $\varepsilon_i(b_1)=0$ and $\varepsilon_i(b_2)\le\langle h_i,wt(b_1)\rangle$ for every $i\in I$; (iii) $\varepsilon_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=0$ for every $i\in I$. In this case $wt(b)=wt(b_1)+wt(b_2)$ is dominant.

(b) **Generated components.** For every highest vertex $b\in B_1\otimes B_2$ of weight $\lambda$, the lowering-generated subcrystal $F(b)$ is a connected component of $B_1\otimes B_2$, is isomorphic as a crystal to the canonical $B(\lambda)=\mathcal B(\lambda)$ of [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]], and $\lambda\in P^+$.

(c) **Decomposition.** $B_1\otimes B_2$ is the disjoint union of the subcrystals $F(b)$ over the highest weight elements $b\in B_1\otimes B_2$, each of which is a highest weight crystal in the sense of [[def-highest-weight-element-and-connected-highest-weight-crystal]]; the multiplicity of $B(\lambda)$ as a component equals the multiplicity of $V(\lambda)$ in the tensor product module $M_1\otimes M_2$.

No choice principle beyond the inherited one is used.

scaffold.statement: The proposed implication is: from the degenerate categorification theorem of this page together with the isomorphism $H^\Lambda_d\cong H^\Lambda_{\xi,d}$ between the degenerate and nondegenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebras, conclude the Ariki categorification theorem for $H^\Lambda_{\xi,d}$ at every parameter $\xi$. **Statement refuted:** once the isomorphism $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] is known, the classes of the word projectives $R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$ are automatically lower global basis vectors; in particular the K_0-level categorification alone identifies the global basis.
**Counterexample (rank two, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$).** Let $I=\{i\}$, $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$. In weight $2\alpha_i$ the word projective is $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)$, which is not indecomposable: by the rank-one case of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] it is a direct sum of $[2]_{q_i}!=(q+q^{-1})$ copies of the self-dual divided-power projective $P_{i,2}$, so its class is
$$[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})\,[P_{i,2}].$$
Under $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(2\Lambda_1)$ the class $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]$ is the ordinary product $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$, while the lower global basis vector in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the divided power $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}=F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}/[2]_{q_i}$; the two differ by the scalar $q+q^{-1}\notin\{\pm q^n\}$, so no K_0-level statement that only names the module $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)$ and its class can decide between them. The lower global basis is picked out only by the additional structure: the self-dual shift normalization of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], bar invariance, and the positivity of the divided-power coefficients, none of which is part of the bare $K_0\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ statement. The example also shows the true positive claim: the lower global class in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the class of the *indecomposable* projective $P_{i,2}$, not of the word projective.
scaffold.strategy: Compute the two classes in the rank-one quotient and compare. (i) $NH_2$ has the PBW basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,x_1^ax_2^b\tau\}$ and $NH_2\cong P_{i,2}^{\oplus[2]_{q_i}!}$ with $[2]_{q_i}!=(q+q^{-1})$ given by the polynomial-column decomposition (KL I Section 2.2 and Section 3.1, quoted in [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]); the cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)$ is a finite-dimensional graded quotient in which the same projective cover decomposition persists with the shift centering $P_{i,2}$ (the projective decomposition is the rank-two case of the divided-power construction, with the cyclotomic quotient acting on the finitely many PBW classes), hence the displayed class identity. (ii) In $U^-_A(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ one has $F_i^2=[2]_{q_i}F_i^{(2)}$ by the definition of the divided power, so under the K_0 isomorphism the word class $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]$ corresponds to $[2]_{q_i}F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$; the lower global basis vector is $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$ by [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] specialized to the rank-one module. For finite-dimensional V over Q(q), let M⊂V be an A=Z[q,q^-1]-submodule spanning V and L0,L∞ full free A0,A∞ lattices. Write E=M∩L0∩L∞. (1) If E→(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0) is a Z-isomorphism, then M∩L0≅Z[q]⊗_Z E, M∩L∞≅Z[q^-1]⊗_Z E and M≅A⊗_Z E; the infinity residue map is also an isomorphism. Rational chart extension gives A0⊗_Z E≅L0 and A∞⊗_Z E≅L∞. If E has a finite Z-basis, these are actual free bases. No containment M⊂L0∩L∞ or freeness of M/E is assumed.
(2) If a Z-module F maps into M∩L0∩L∞, generates M over A, and maps injectively into both rational residues L0/qL0 and L∞/q^-1L∞, then F≅E≅(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0).
(3) More generally let N⊂M be an A-submodule with integral balanced intersection E_N=N∩L0∩L∞. If a Z-module F maps to M∩(L0+N)∩(L∞+N), generates M modulo N over A, and maps injectively into (L0+Q N)/(qL0+Q N) and (L∞+Q N)/(q^-1L∞+Q N), then M is balanced. The sequence 0→(N∩L0)/(N∩qL0)→(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0)→(L0+Q N)/(qL0+Q N) is exact, and the last image is the image of F. If F and E_N are finite free Z-modules, so is E_M, and M is free over A. These are Kashiwara91 Lemmas7.1.1–7.1.2, in integral notation; their rational base extension gives the usual Q[q±] criterion.
scaffold.strategy:
(1) E injects into the rational residue by the hypothesis, hence is Z-torsionfree. Residue surjectivity gives M∩L0⊂Σ_(k=0)^n q^k E+M∩q^(n+1)L0 for every n, by repeatedly subtracting a lift and dividing by q (which preserves M). For x also in q^nL∞, the subtracted terms k≤n lie there; the remainder is in q^n(M∩qL0∩L∞)=0 by residue injectivity on E. Thus M∩L0∩q^nL∞=⊕_(k=0)^n q^kE. Every element of M∩L0 has a finite infinity-pole bound, so the union over n gives Z[q]E. Distinct powers are independent: in a finite relation normalize the lowest exponent and reduce modulo q, then successively remove it. Also M=Z[q±](M∩L0) by finite zero-pole bounds. The analogous infinity-pole argument gives Z[q^-1]E and the mirror residue isomorphism. Since M spans V, Q(q)E spans V; rational residue injection shows a Q-basis of QE is independent and full. Expanding in that basis, zero/infinity valuation gives the full chart extension identities. Freeness over A is claimed only if E is actually finite free over Z.
(2) Laurent expansions in phi(F) have unique finite coefficients: reduce the lowest exponent at0 using the first injection. If an expansion lies in L0 it has no negative exponent; if it lies in L∞ it has no positive exponent, by the second injection. Therefore the intersection is exactly phi(F), with the claimed residue map and factorization. This is finite Laurent linear algebra, not passage to an unjustified formal limit.
(3) Work first on each finitely generated submodule F′ of F; its rational residue injection implies Z-torsionfreeness and hence finite Z-freeness. The balanced factorization of N gives N=(N∩L0)+(N∩L∞). If x∈M∩(L0+N)∩(L∞+N), subtract an element of N to put it in L0. Its remaining discrepancy from L∞ lies in N; split that discrepancy into its zero and infinity chart parts, then subtract its zero chart part to obtain an element of M∩L0∩L∞. Thus the lifts of a finite Z-basis of F′ can be changed by N so that they lie in the simultaneous intersection. Their direct sum with E_N injects into each rational residue: in the quotient modulo QN the F′ component is forced0 by the assumed injection, and then E_N injectivity forces the remaining component0. They generate AF′+N over A. Apply (2) to obtain balancedness and the exact residue sequence there. Taking the union over finite F′ proves the general assertion, without claiming an infinite torsionfree Z-module is free. When F and E_N are finite free, the direct sum description gives E_M finite free. This reproduces the printed diagrams and avoids the native unsupported chart containment, wrong q^nL0/q^nL∞ recursion and coherent-sheaf freeness shortcut.

Finite projective Hom duality commutes with this basechange, and finite vector duality commutes with inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels $h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and $T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_B S)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Tensor a shifted-free retract to prove finite projectivity. Every degree-zero endomorphism of $B\otimes P$ lifts through $P\to B\otimes P$ by generic projectivity; endomorphisms preserve $JP$, so this is a surjective endomorphism-ring homomorphism. Its domain is local for indecomposable $P$, hence a nonzero quotient is indecomposable. If $JS=0$, the old cover factors through $P/JP$ and remains essential: pull back a submodule and use the old superfluous kernel. If $JS\ne0$ and $P/JP\ne0$, finite dimension supplies a simple quotient, which must be the old unique head $S$, contradicting its being annihilated by $J$. Every $B$-simple inflates to a generic simple; its descended cover therefore exhausts the projective basis, proving surjectivity and no merging.
For finite $P$, evaluation on a shifted-free module and restriction to retracts gives $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B\otimes P,B)=\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,A)\otimes_A B$. Applying $\psi$ gives $(B\otimes P)^\#=B\otimes P^\#$. Inflation does not change $D_\psi S$. Use only the choice-free finite-module normalization clauses of the generic positive-divided-string supplier. They yield the unique self-dual representatives; no conditional quantum-global clause is used.
Finally $h(P,S)=T(P^\#,S)$ by finite-projective evaluation and $D(P^\psi\otimes S)=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,D_\psi S)$ by evaluation of a tensor functional. A normalized cover has $h(P,S)=q^a$ because absolute $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$. Both dualities fix the normalized labels, so $q^a=q^{-a}$ and $a=0$. Other simple heads have zero Hom. Shift-orbit bases now make both normalized pairings perfect. This proof distinguishes projective Hom duality from vector duality and never uses a symmetric trace.

It intertwines the CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is $\Psi_{\rm KK}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\rm can}|_\beta$. scaffold.statement: Let $M=\mathbb C^2$ be the trivial $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$-module, $V=\mathbb C^2$ the natural module and $d=1$. The Arakawa-Suzuki construction provides an action of $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$ on $M\otimes V\cong\mathbb C^4$ commuting with $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, but here $x_1=\Omega^{M,V}=0$, so the action is the evaluation action $x_1\mapsto0$ and $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(\mathbb C^4)=M_4(\mathbb C)$. On the other hand the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ in $\mathrm{End}(M\otimes V)$ is the subalgebra $1_{\mathbb C^2}\otimes M_2(\mathbb C)$, of dimension $4$. Hence the equality $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=\mathrm{End}_{H_d}(M\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ fails by a factor of $4$ in dimension, even though the Hecke action is genuine, commutes with $\mathfrak g$, and is natural in $M$. The other equality also fails: $\psi(H_1)=\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}\subsetneq\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(M\otimes V)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\otimes1$, of dimension $4$. The hypothesis that is missing is the truncated/deformed setup: the double centralizer theorem applies to the finite-W-algebra tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ over the pyramid (equivalently to $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ with the truncated polynomial algebra $C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$), where the Hecke action is the cyclotomic quotient action and the algebra of the opposite side is the finite W-algebra, not $U(\mathfrak g)$.

This is not a counterexample to the higher-level Schur-Weyl theorem: it shows that the theorem needs the finite-W-algebra deformation/truncation hypotheses, and that a mere commuting Hecke action on an arbitrary tensor module is insufficient.

scaffold.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$ (so $l=1$, two parts equal to $1$) and $d=3$: the stable range fails, because at least $3$ parts of $\lambda$ equal to $1$ is false. Here $H_3(\Lambda)=\mathbb C[S_3]$ (level $l=1$), of dimension $6$, while the image $H_3(\lambda,c)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}$, $V=\mathbb C^2$, has dimension $5$: for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $V^{\otimes3}=L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$, so $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ has dimension $1+4=5$, and it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Under the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ (trivial, sign and standard blocks), the map to $\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ kills exactly the sign block; hence $H_3(\lambda,c)\cong f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ with $f$ the central idempotent of the trivial and standard blocks, and $f$ is the block idempotent corner of the Definition. Verify: $\dim f\mathbb C[S_3]f=1+4=5$, the map $\mathbb C[S_3]\twoheadrightarrow f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ is multiplication by $f$, and the antisymmetrizer $a=\sum_{w\in S_3}\mathrm{sgn}(w)w$ spans the kernel of the action on $V^{\otimes3}$ because $\Lambda^3V=0$ for $\dim V=2$.
scaffold.strategy: Decompose $V^{\otimes3}$ for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ by the classical Schur-Weyl rule: the partitions of $3$ with at most $2$ rows are $(3)$ and $(2,1)$, so $V^{\otimes3}\cong L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$; hence $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})\cong\mathbb C\times M_2$, of dimension $5$, and by Schur-Weyl duality it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Compare with the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2$: the sign block acts on $V^{\otimes3}$ by zero because the sign representation does not occur in $V^{\otimes3}$ (equivalently $\Lambda^3V=0$), so the kernel is the sign block and the image is the corner of the other two blocks. The dimension count and the corner identification verify the general statement of the preceding Definition in the smallest non-stable case.

1. The rank-zero algebra is $k$ and restriction from root zero has zero target, so the vacuum is nonzero and killed by every $E_i$; its weight is $\Lambda$.
2. The finitely many word idempotents sum to the unit of each finite root block. Every finite projective is a retract of finitely many shifted copies of their principal projectives. The append bimodule sends the word $\nu$ to $\nu i$; hence composition acts from the rightmost functor first and gives the displayed reversed operator order.
3. The quotient-cover lemma says every cyclotomic indecomposable cover is the extension of its normalized generic cover. Therefore extension of scalars is surjective on split $K_0$. The GENERIC negative-half categorification identifies generic $K_0$ with $U_A^-$, generated as an $A$-module by products of the actual divided-power projectives. Their extensions are the cyclotomic divided functors on the vacuum, so these divided words span. This does not divide by a quantum factorial: $F_i^a=[a]_{q_i}!F_i^{(a)}$ has a generally nonunit coefficient. Combining generation with the independent normalized-action supplier proves the highest-weight claim without a circular appeal to the integral highest-weight theorem.

scaffold.statement: The characteristic-zero theorems of this page ([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]], [[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]) compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis coefficients. Consequently the characteristic-zero canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the boundary recorded in [[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]] and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.

scaffold.statement:
For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any field and any real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, put $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$, and $q_i=q^{d_i}$. On projective $K_0$ use $F_i=F_i^{\rm basic}$ and $E_i|_\beta=q_i^{-1-h_i(\beta)}E_i^{\rm basic}$; on module $G_0$ use either the SAME canonical normalization, or the Kang--Kashiwara normalization $E_i^{\rm KK}=E_i^{\rm basic}$, $F_i^{\rm KK}|_\beta=q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}F_i^{\rm basic}$. In all cases $K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$. These operators satisfy the full quantum mixed and Serre relations and are locally nilpotent; their scalar extensions to $\mathbb Q(q)$ are integrable weight modules. No decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules is asserted in affine or indefinite type.
The tensor pairing $T_\beta(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M)$ is $A$-BILINEAR and weightwise perfect in normalized projective-cover/simple bases. The Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ instead satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ and is first-bar-sesquilinear. For $T$, projective $E_i$ is adjoint to module $F_i^{\rm KK}$ and projective $F_i$ to module $E_i^{\rm KK}$. The two module actions are conjugate by the weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$, where $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$.
scaffold.strategy:
1. The normalized-action supplier combines the actual same-color categorical decomposition and unequal-color mixed crossings with finite root strings. For $E_i$ applied to input root $\beta+\alpha_i$ its exponent is $-1-h_i(\beta+\alpha_i)=1-h_i(\beta)$, exactly the target-weight normalization. Its general rank-one Hom-envelope proof gives every symmetrizable Serre relation without a rank-two finite-orbit assumption.
2. Tensor products of finite modules are finite, hence $T$ has Laurent-polynomial values. The quotient-cover lemma gives absolutely simple normalized heads and $T(P(S),S')=\delta_{S,S'}$, proving weightwise perfectness. Shifting either tensor factor multiplies by the same $q$-power; this is bilinearity, whereas finite-projective evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ with $(P^\#)^\psi\otimes M$, giving the different Hom convention.
3. For the corner $A_\beta\to eB_{\beta+i}e$, associativity gives $T_B(FP,M)=T_A(P,EM)$ for the BASIC functors. The generator-fixing anti-involution flips balanced tensors, so $T_B(P,FM)=T_A(EP,M)$ as well: the corner factors become $eB$ and $Be$ in opposite order and multiplication gives the evaluation isomorphism. Multiplying the second identity by $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}$ gives the first normalized adjoint statement; the first identity gives the other. This uses neither the Frobenius theorem nor the highest-weight $K_0$ theorem.
4. Adding $i$ changes defect by $d_i(h_i(\beta)-1)$. Consequently multiplication by $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$ conjugates the canonical module action to the KK action in both directions. The weight action is unchanged. All assertions here are about the standard homogeneous quotient, not arbitrary monic deformations.

scaffold.statement:
**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP) $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written $\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]].

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$ is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]), and $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks ([[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the same $e$ and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series ([[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]); a different series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus $\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter, equal to the source's $\xi$) and $q$ (the grading variable, equal to the source's quantum variable) are INDEPENDENT data; the design's phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of a square $q_{\rm src}^2$, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model $\mathcal F_{\rm sym}$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge $0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$, basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$, empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary Dipper–James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Define $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is $\theta$-pullback of $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative Jucys–Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block. At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem [[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]] identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains outside the present nondegenerate regime.

No choice principle is used.
scaffold.strategy: Direct convention check. At level one $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; the finite-characteristic hypothesis $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ makes $\xi\ne1$ a primitive $e$-th root, and in sub-branch (CP) the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ is exactly what makes a primitive $e$-th root exist in $F$. The type-$A$ datum and the grading are batch-24 clauses; the transport statement is the graded block isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock-side residues, the restricted labels and the empty component are batch-9/batch-23 clauses. The ordinary dictionary uses the actual universal module-and-form comparison [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]], not a rename of a cellular module. Its Laurent-unit form factor preserves radicals, including zero quotients, and gives $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}\cong(D_{\rm M}^{\lambda})^{\theta}$; apply the involution again. Right-to-left conversion sends $h\cdot m=m h^*$, and commutation $\theta *=*\theta$ preserves the same pullback dictionary. On the finite level-one tower $X_j=\xi^{1-j}T_{j-1}\cdots T_1^2\cdots T_{j-1}$. Applying $\theta(T_r)=-\xi T_r^{-1}$ to this palindrome gives $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$: the $2j-2$ signs cancel and the scalar is $\xi^{j-1}$. Generalized eigenvalues $\xi^i$ therefore become $\xi^{-i}$, proving the content reflection. No raw Hecke automorphism is claimed to preserve a fixed transported grading. The $\xi=1$ specialization is the separate arbitrary-field polytabloid specialization corollary, not an inference from a prime-field-only statement. The parameter dictionary is the naming clause of [BK 2009 §1 and §4.2] and [Ariki 1996 §1]; it makes no substitution. No choice is used.

For rank one $d_i=1$ and $\lambda\ge1$, let $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$ and $P=B$. The PROJECTIVE Hom dual satisfies $P^\#\cong P$, so the canonical normalized projective is $P$ with no shift. Its finite vector dual is different:
$$D_\psi P\cong P\{-2(\lambda-1)\}.$$
The unique vector-dual-centered shift of this regular module is $P\{-(\lambda-1)\}$. For $\lambda=1$ both centers agree; for $\lambda=2$, projective Hom-self-duality centers $P$ at $0$ while vector-self-duality centers it at $-1$. If $\lambda=0$ the block is zero and there is no indecomposable projective here. For any normalized cyclotomic projective the general relation is $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$; it does not redefine the lower-basis projective normalization.
scaffold.strategy: Evaluation $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,B)\cong B$ gives the projective dual directly, with the generator-fixing anti-involution producing the same left module. The coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda-1}$ trace has degree $-2(\lambda-1)$ and its perfect anti-diagonal pairing identifies $D_\psi B$ with $B$ in that NEGATIVE shift. Since $D_\psi(P\{s\})=D_\psi P\{-s\}$, vector self-duality solves $-2(\lambda-1)-s=s$, namely $s=-(\lambda-1)$. Projective Hom self-duality instead solves $-s=s$, namely $s=0$. These distinct finite calculations establish uniqueness of each center and their stated examples. The symmetric-algebra theorem gives the general defect shift after the independent projective normalization; no trace halving is used to pick the lower-basis class.

Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift $M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. It therefore induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and $G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed anti-automorphisms $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$ (i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective Hom-dualities $\#$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives.

**Application.** For each nonzero content sector choose the actual graded block isomorphism rho_alpha. DEFINE the Hecke duality by star_H=rho_alpha star_R rho_alpha^{-1}. This is a grading-preserving anti-involution, fixing the NAMED images of e(i),y_r,psi_r, and rho_alpha intertwines it by definition. Thus the preceding duality conclusion applies blockwise. This does not identify star_H with the raw cellular anti-involution that fixes affine Hecke generators, and does not infer that a product is fixed merely because its factors are fixed.

No choice.

Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module** $$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$ a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$ fix a reduced decomposition $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put $z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov-Lauda presentation of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]. The definition asserts, and proves below in [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of $S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_T q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** This is the LEFT Murphy cell module, obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=m h^*$. Separately, [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]] gives $S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after the same left-module conversion. The labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

scaffold.statement:
Fix the level-one type-A integer KLR presentation, charge $0$, and finite quantum characteristic $e\in\{2,3,\ldots\}$. Let $K$ be any characteristic-zero field in the specified Hecke regime, let $\lambda$ be the specified partition, and let $S_K(\lambda)$ be the LEFT graded Murphy cell Specht module with its specified initial cyclic generator $z_K$. Then there is a finite-dimensional graded module $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ for the rational KLR algebra, with a specified homogeneous cyclic vector $z_{\mathbb Q}$, and a graded generator-preserving isomorphism $K\otimes_{\mathbb Q} S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)\cong S_K(\lambda)$. The rational module is explicitly presented by the initial weight, dot and horizontal crossing relations, together with one homogeneous rational relation for each Garnir belt. Each of these relations is the unique vector with Garnir coefficient $1$ in the kernel of a finite matrix with integer entries, obtained from crossing operators in the integer row permutation module. It therefore depends only on the integer presentation, not on a choice of $K$ or of a root of unity.

If the specified normalized simple head $D_K(\lambda)$ is nonzero and absolutely simple, this construction, combined with the local cyclic-head descent lemma, defines its initial-generator image line over $\mathbb Q$ up to scalar. The orbit of that image under the finite integer cyclotomic algebra is a lattice of rank $\dim_K D_K(\lambda)$.
scaffold.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] gives the affine KLR PBW basis. Dot slides remove one crossing from correction terms, quadratic moves remove two, and three-term braid corrections remove three. Preferred reduced expressions differ by terms with strictly fewer crossings.

[F2] [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] fixes the integer coefficients and the source BK/BKW crossing convention $\psi=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$. This proof uses that convention directly; it does not identify KMR's reversed-orientation crossing with it.

[F3] [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] supplies the LEFT Murphy cell Specht module's homogeneous standard basis $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_K$ and triangularity: for every tableau $T$, $v_T$ is a combination of standard $v_U$ with $w_U\le w_T$ in strong Bruhat order. Idempotents and grading restrict this expansion to the vector's weight and degree.

[F4] The specified initial vector has weight $i^\lambda$, all dots kill it, and a crossing kills it when its two successive entries occupy the same initial row. These are the initial-generator relations in the reviewed BKW construction, not conditions imposed on an arbitrary vector in a simple.

[F5] [[lem-integer-cyclic-presentation-descends-the-simple-head-generator-line]] proves characteristic-zero radical base change by the regular trace pairing, hence descends a rational cyclic module's normalized simple head and its specified generator image, and proves the lattice rank.

[F6] [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]] gives the finite free integer cyclotomic algebra used in step 5.2. The local PBW straightening used before that quotient is integral: its monic moves have integer coefficients, and independence follows by rational scalar extension of the supplied PBW basis.

## Proof

**Given:** The stated level-one integer presentation, the specified LEFT cell module and its initial generator, and F1–F5. No Axiom of Choice is used.

1.1 Put $\kappa=0$ in the residue formulas below. Work first in the affine content algebra $R_{\mathbb Z}$ before the cyclotomic quotient. For each row of $\lambda$, the successive residue segment has a one-dimensional integral module on which its word idempotent is $1$ and its dots and internal crossings are $0$. The KLR relations hold: successive colours are distinct, their quadratic at zero dots is $0$, and a possible three-strand repeated-endpoint pattern occurs only for $e=2$, where its double-edge braid correction also vanishes at zero dots. Induce the tensor product of these segment modules, and shift its generator $m_0$ to degree $\deg(T_0)$, where $T_0$ is row reading. Denote the result by $M_{\mathbb Z}$. [F2, construct, algebra]

1.2 Let $P$ be the Young row subgroup. Choose reduced expressions compatible with the unique decomposition $w=d p$, with $d$ a minimal representative for $S_d/P$ and $p\in P$, and $\ell(w)=\ell(d)+\ell(p)$. F1 then makes the inducing bimodule free over the row algebra on the minimal-representative words. Tensoring the one-dimensional row modules shows that $M_{\mathbb Z}$ has the integral basis $m_T=\psi_{w_T}m_0$ indexed by all row-strict tableaux $T$. Its cyclic presentation is exactly the initial weight, dot and horizontal-crossing relations. In particular all generator-action matrices on this finite basis have integer entries. Put $M_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes M_{\mathbb Z}$; scalar extension gives $M_K=K\otimes M_{\mathbb Q}$. By F4, there is a surjective graded map $\pi_K:M_K\to S_K(\lambda)$ carrying $m_0$ exactly to $z_K$. [F1, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

1.3 Crossing straightening gives a filtration useful below: a word with at most $N$ crossings applied to $m_0$ is a combination of $m_U$ with $\ell(w_U)\le N$. Move dots right, reduce nonreduced words by quadratic and Coxeter moves, compare reduced words, and split off the right row subgroup as in step 1.2. Positive dot powers kill $m_0$; a nontrivial row factor ends in an internal crossing and also kills $m_0$. Every correction has fewer crossings. In particular if $s_rT$ is row-strict and $\ell(w_{s_rT})=\ell(w_T)+1$, then $\psi_r m_T=m_{s_rT}$ plus terms of strictly smaller crossing length, with leading coefficient exactly $1$. If $s_rT$ is not row-strict, its possible leading term is killed by the right row factor and only shorter terms remain. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 Fix a Garnir node $A=(a,b)$ with $(a+1,b)\in\lambda$. Its belt consists of the row-$a$ suffix $X$ beginning at column $b$ and row-$(a+1)$ prefix $Y$ ending at column $b$. The entries in these nodes in $T_0$ form one consecutive interval $J=\{u,\ldots,v\}$: the suffix ends at the last position of row $a$, immediately followed by the prefix at the beginning of row $a+1$. Let $G_A$ agree with $T_0$ outside the belt and fill $Y$ first, then $X$, increasingly with $J$. It is row-strict and nonstandard. This $G_A$ is the nonstandard belt filling used for the rational-kernel presentation; it is distinct from the maximal STANDARD Garnir tableau in [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]. [construct, algebra]

2.2 Among ALL row-strict tableaux agreeing with $T_0$ outside this belt, $G_A$ is the only nonstandard one. For columns $c<b$, the upper entry is an unchanged number less than $u$, hence less than every changed lower entry. For columns $c>b$, the lower entry, if present, is unchanged and greater than $v$, hence greater than every changed upper entry. Comparisons with the row above or the row below have the same strict bounds, and every other column comparison is unchanged. Thus only column $b$ can fail. It fails precisely when the first upper-belt entry exceeds the last lower-belt entry. Since each of the two rows is increasing, this is equivalent to every upper-belt entry exceeding every lower-belt entry, and hence to the unique filling $G_A$. [step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 On $J$, the residue word $i(G_A)$ is one successive-residue segment. Along $Y$ the residues increase by $1$; its final node $(a+1,b)$ has residue $\kappa+b-a-1$. The first node of $X$, $(a,b)$, has residue $\kappa+b-a$, and the rest again increase by $1$. Consequently $i(G_A)_r\ne i(G_A)_{r+1}$ for every $u\le r<v$, including $e=2$. This distinctness, rather than any braid normalization, is essential. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

2.4 Let $\delta_A=\deg(\psi_{w_{G_A}}e(i^\lambda))+\deg(T_0)$ and let $T_A^{\mathbb Q}$ be the span of those integral basis vectors $m_T$ for which $T$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt, has weight $i(G_A)$, and has homogeneous degree $\delta_A$. It includes $m_{G_A}$. The use of the entire weight-degree slice avoids any brick-classification assumption. Write $T_A^K=K\otimes T_A^{\mathbb Q}$. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct]

2.5 The vector $\pi_K(m_{G_A})$ is a combination of images of standard basis vectors in $T_A^K$. Indeed F3 gives standard $U$ with $w_U\le w_{G_A}$. The permutation $w_{G_A}$ belongs to the parabolic subgroup generated by $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$, since it permutes only $J$. Every Bruhat-smaller permutation belongs to this same subgroup: choose a reduced word for $w_{G_A}$ in these generators, and use the defining subword characterization of strong Bruhat order. Hence $U$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt. Weight idempotents discard different words, and homogeneity discards different degrees, leaving exactly the standard vectors in the slice of step 2.4. By step 2.2, every other vector of the slice is standard; by F3 its image is part of the standard Specht basis and is linearly independent. Therefore $\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$ is precisely one-dimensional, including the case where the image of $m_{G_A}$ is zero. [F3, step 2.2, step 2.4, algebra]

3.1 For every $u\le r<v$, the image $\psi_r T_A^K$ in $M_K$ is spanned by standard row-strict belt tableaux. To see the support assertion, choose reduced words for all belt permutations using only $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$. Straightening a crossing supported in this interval never introduces a crossing outside it; factoring a right row permutation also uses only this interval. Thus every resulting row-strict basis tableau agrees outside the belt. The image has fixed weight $s_r i(G_A)$, which differs from $i(G_A)$ by step 2.3. Its support cannot include the sole nonstandard belt tableau $G_A$. Hence the entire image has standard support by step 2.2, and $\pi_K$ is injective on its span by F3. [F1, F3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 2.4, algebra]

3.2 If $x\in\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$, then $\pi_K(\psi_r x)=\psi_r\pi_K(x)=0$. The injectivity in step 3.1 implies $\psi_r x=0$ in $M_K$ for every inside-belt crossing. Thus this one-dimensional Specht-kernel line lies in $B_A^K:=\bigcap_{r=u}^{v-1}\ker(\psi_r:T_A^K\to M_K)$. [step 2.5, step 3.1, algebra]

3.3 The $m_{G_A}$ coefficient map is injective on $B_A^K$. Suppose a nonzero $x\in B_A^K$ has that coefficient zero. Choose a tableau $T$ with nonzero coefficient in $x$ whose crossing length $N=\ell(w_T)$ is maximal. It is standard by step 2.2. Record membership in $X$ or $Y$ for the successive numbers $u,\ldots,v$ as a binary word. Unless this word is all $Y$ then all $X$, it has an adjacent occurrence $XY$; that excluded word is exactly $G_A$. Choose such an occurrence at $r,r+1$. Swapping them preserves row strictness because they lie in different rows and are consecutive numbers; it increases permutation length by $1$, because $r$ is in the earlier row. Its weight becomes $s_r i(G_A)\ne i(G_A)$, so it cannot be $G_A$ and is also standard by step 2.2. By step 1.3, the coefficient of $m_{s_rT}$ in $\psi_r x$ at length $N+1$ is precisely the nonzero coefficient of $m_T$ in $x$. A lower-length input cannot reach length $N+1$; a different equal-length input has a different possible leading tableau because $s_r$ is injective; and its correction terms have smaller length. Therefore $\psi_r x\ne0$, contradicting $x\in B_A^K$. [step 1.3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.2, algebra]

3.4 Consequently $\dim_K B_A^K\le1$, while step 3.2 gives a nonzero line inside it. Thus $B_A^K=\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$. Define $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ using the same intersection of crossing kernels over $\mathbb Q$. These are kernels of a single finite stacked matrix with integer entries on the explicitly selected integral row-strict bases. Row reduction over $\mathbb Q$ commutes with extension to $K$, so $B_A^K=K\otimes B_A^{\mathbb Q}$. It follows that $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ is one-dimensional and has a unique rational vector $h_A$ with coefficient $1$ on $m_{G_A}$. Its scalar extension is exactly the Specht-kernel vector with that normalization. This is an explicit rational linear-system construction of the relation, not an assumption that a chosen vector belongs to a rational form. [step 1.2, step 3.2, step 3.3, algebra]

4.1 Every other row-strict belt tableau has strictly smaller crossing length than $G_A$. Outside the belt there are no inversions involving belt entries because the belt interval is consecutive in row reading and its values form $J$. Inside, inversions are exactly upper/lower pairs with the upper entry larger. The tableau $G_A$ has all $|X||Y|$ such inversions, whereas every other filling loses at least one. Hence $h_A=m_{G_A}+\sum_{U:\,\ell(w_U)<\ell(w_{G_A})}c_U m_U$ with rational $c_U$, and it is homogeneous of degree $\delta_A$ by its definition in the slice. [step 2.1, step 2.4, step 3.4, algebra]

4.2 Put $S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}=M_{\mathbb Q}/\sum_A R_{\mathbb Q}h_A$. We prove standard spanning locally. For any nonstandard row-strict $T$, choose a vertical inversion at $(a,b),(a+1,b)$. All entries in its upper suffix $X$ exceed all entries in its lower prefix $Y$. Its Garnir factor $G_A$ therefore satisfies $T=wG_A$ with $w=w_Tw_{G_A}^{-1}$ and $\ell(w)=\ell(w_T)-\ell(w_{G_A})$: reordering the contiguous belt's one-line list from $X,Y$ to $Y,X$ removes precisely its $|X||Y|$ cross inversions, while preserving within-part and outside comparisons. Reduced-word straightening and the relation $h_A=0$ replace $m_T$ by words with fewer than $\ell(w_T)$ crossings, by step 4.1. The filtration of step 1.3 expresses these as row-strict vectors of strictly smaller length. Induction proves that standard vectors span the quotient. [F1, step 1.3, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

4.3 Scalar extension of the rational quotient presentation gives $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}=K\otimes S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}$. Every $h_A$ lies in $\ker\pi_K$ by step 3.4, so $\pi_K$ induces a surjection $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}\to S_K(\lambda)$ preserving the generator and grading. The source is spanned by the standard vectors by step 4.2, and their images are the linearly independent standard Specht basis by F3. Hence this map is an isomorphism. In particular the rational module is finite-dimensional, has its standard basis, and its generator maps exactly to $z_K$. [F3, step 3.4, step 4.2, algebra]

5.1 The rational module factors through the cyclotomic quotient. Each specified cyclotomic relation acts as zero after extension to $K$, because the module in step 4.3 is the specified cyclotomic Hecke cell Specht module. The matrix of that action on the rational standard basis has rational entries; faithful field extension forces it to be zero already over $\mathbb Q$. Denote this rational cyclotomic module by $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$, with generator $z_{\mathbb Q}$ the class of $m_0$. This identifies the required rational initial cyclic generator, not merely the unpointed module's isomorphism class. [step 4.3, algebra]

5.2 If an integer cyclic quotient is desired for F5, take the saturated generator annihilator $I_{\mathbb Z}=\{a\in A_{\mathbb Z}:a z_{\mathbb Q}=0\}$ in the finite integer cyclotomic algebra of [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]]. It is a homogeneous left ideal, and $A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z}$ identifies with the integral orbit $A_{\mathbb Z}z_{\mathbb Q}\subset S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$. Its rational span is the entire rational module by cyclicity, so $\mathbb Q\otimes(A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z})\cong S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ with the specified generator. Clearing denominators in each $h_A$ is also possible, but no unsaturated integer quotient or integral Specht-freeness theorem is needed. [step 5.1, algebra]

5.3 Apply F5 to this pointed rational form and the supplied absolutely simple normalized head. Its radical-basechange proof gives a rational normalized head with the image of $z_{\mathbb Q}$; absolute Schur makes every quotient map to the fixed head differ only by a scalar. Its integral-algebra orbit is finitely generated and torsion-free, with rational span that head, so its rank is exactly the head's $K$-dimension. This establishes the precise requested initial-generator line and lattice statement over arbitrary characteristic-zero $K$. No three-brick identity, unproved R-matrix formula, arbitrary-vector rational form, or change of the specified generator enters the argument. [F5, step 5.1, step 5.2, algebra] ∎

In the situation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. both tableaux are standard, $S=s_rT$, and $r$ occupies an earlier row-reading node than $r+1$, as in [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]), then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the Cartan matrix of the regime.
2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition, then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$ in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].
3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and $S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.

All steps are finite residue and brick computations; no choice. For the strict Garnir case retain the maximal standard belt tableau and strict Bruhat lower condition. Reduce to a two-row belt ending at its final node by the agreement-outside-belt lemma. Remove complete horizontal e-bricks using the ABOVE codegree lemma. The lower tableau has residual codegree -1 if b is nonzero modulo e and 0 otherwise. The Garnir tableau has codegree0/1 for e>2, and1/2 for e=2, respectively. Their difference gives degree1/2 in the single/double-edge cases. Equal-color degree in a standard exchange remains -2, from the Cartan diagonal; it is not assigned +2.

If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced decompositions of the same $w_T$, then $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\unlhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$; in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is independent of the choices.

scaffold.statement:
**Statement refuted.** Let $M$ be a weight module with a $U_A$-stable lattice and $\bar M$ its specialization at $q\mapsto1$. Then the operator induced by an element $x\in U_A$ is computed by substituting $q=1$ into any expression of $x$ as a rational function of $q$ with coefficients in $U_A$, numerator and denominator specializing separately.

**Counterexample.** In the rank-one quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ take $x=[K;0]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}=T_{0,1}\in U_A$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). The numerator $K-K^{-1}$ and the denominator $q-q^{-1}$ both vanish under the substitution $K\mapsto1$, $q\mapsto1$, so the naive rule gives the undefined symbol $0/0$. The actual specialization is the coroot label: on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the operator $x$ acts by $[\mu(h)]_q\mapsto\mu(h)$, which is generally nonzero ([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]](ii)). Concretely, on the two-dimensional module $L(1)$ with $K=\mathrm{diag}(q,q^{-1})$ and basis $v_0,v_1$, $x$ acts as $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$, whereas substituting $q=1$ into $K$ gives the identity operator: the naive substitution loses the entire Cartan action. The same failure occurs for the divided-power commutation coefficients $\frac{1}{q^b-q^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1})$ of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii), whose denominator vanishes at $q=1$ while the operator specializes to the finite value given by the string formula, and for the Gaussian-binomial expression $[m]_q=\frac{q^m-q^{-m}}{q-q^{-1}}$, whose naive value at $q=1$ is again $0/0$ although the correct specialization is the integer $m$. The repair is the integral-form statement of [[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]]: specialization is defined on elements of $U_A$ (and on lattice operators), not by substituting into rational expressions.
scaffold.strategy:
Step 1 (the element and its two evaluations). $x=T_{0,1}\in U_A$ is a generator of the integral form; on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ it acts by the scalar $[\mu(d_ih_i)]_{q_i}=[\mu(h_i)]_i$, which at $q\mapsto1$ is the integer $\mu(h_i)$. The naive substitution $K\mapsto1$, $q\mapsto1$ into $(K-K^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ is $0/0$: both $K-K^{-1}$ and $q-q^{-1}$ specialize to $0$, and no value is defined by separate substitution. This refutes the displayed general principle.

Step 2 (explicit witness). In the two-dimensional module of [[ex-quantum-verma-and-simple-modules-for-sl-two]] with $m=1$, $K$ acts as $\mathrm{diag}(q,q^{-1})$ and $x=T_{0,1}$ as $\mathrm{diag}([1]_q,[-1]_q)=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$; the specialization of $x$ is $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$, a nonzero operator, while the substitution $q=1$ into $K$ yields the identity. Hence the operator induced by $x$ is not obtained by substituting $q=1$ into the expression for $x$.

Step 3 (further witnesses). $[m]_q=(q^m-q^{-m})/(q-q^{-1})$: numerator and denominator vanish at $q=1$, while the correct specialization is the polynomial value $m$ ([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]](ii)); the divided-power coefficient $\frac{1}{q^b-q^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1})$ vanishes in numerator and denominator at $q=1$ yet acts on a weight vector $w$ of weight $\mu$ with $E_iw=0$ by the finite value $[\mu(h_i)-b+1]_i\mapsto\mu(h_i)-b+1$, as the string formula $E_iF_i^{(b)}w=[\mu(h_i)-b+1]_iF_i^{(b-1)}w$ shows by the geometric-sum identity. Each of these is an element of $U_A$ whose value at $q=1$ is defined through the integral form, not through term-by-term substitution.

Step 4 (correct statement). By [[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]], the specialization is the base change $U_A\otimes_Ak$ with $q\mapsto1$, which is well defined because the generators of $U_A$ are actual elements (and the operator matrices on lattice modules are polynomial); the cancellations in Steps 1-3 are handled inside $U_A$. No choice is used.
