scaffold.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group with no imaginary simple roots, so $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and $K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and put $A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]).

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**
$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$
the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}=1$. Each factor is defined in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so $T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$; in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another.

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra
$$U_A:=\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle\subseteq U_q(\mathfrak g),$$
where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$ for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and the $F_i^{(r)}$, and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$, it is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)=U_q(\mathfrak g)$. The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the divided-power reordering identity of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at $q=1$ of these elements are computed in [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]], and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated only after this definition. No freeness, integrality of choices or triangularity is asserted here.
scaffold.strategy: A definition with its integrality conventions fixed. $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ is a subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$, and it is not a principal ideal domain (for example (2,q-1) is not principal). No torsion-free-to-free inference over this ring is permitted. Every $T_{i,c,t}$ is a finite product of elements of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: each numerator is a difference of two toral monomials and each denominator $q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}$ is a nonzero element of the field $\mathbb Q(q)$ because $q$ is transcendental and $d_i>0$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Hence each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$, so the toral elements commute with each other and with all $K_h$; this commutativity is used in the reordering lemma. The generators are homogeneous: $E_i^{(r)}$ has root degree $r\alpha_i$, $F_i^{(r)}$ has degree $-r\alpha_i$, and $K_h,T_{i,c,t}$ have degree $0$; therefore $U_A$ is generated by homogeneous elements and is graded by $Q$, and its intersection with $U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule. Since $E_i,F_i,K_h$ generate $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ as a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra, the $\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. No choice principle is used, and no claim is made here about which products of these generators are independent: the division into the three subalgebras is the subject of the triangular-decomposition theorem.

Work in the rank-one subalgebra $A_i$ generated by $E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $K^{\pm1}=K_i^{\pm1}$ inside $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, with $q=q_i$ and $[m]=[m]_i$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]).

(a) **Divided powers multiply.** $E^{(2)}E^{(1)}=[3]E^{(3)}$ and $F^{(2)}F^{(2)}=[4]![2]!\,F^{(4)}/4!$-free form $F^{(2)}F^{(2)}=\binom{4}{2}_iF^{(4)}$, since $x^{(a)}x^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_ix^{(a+b)}$; numerically, with $q$ transcendental, $\binom{4}{2}_i=(q^2+q^{-2}+1+q^2+q^{-2}+\ldots)$ is a nonzero element of $A$.

(b) **The commutator is the first toral binomial.** $E^{(1)}F^{(1)}-F^{(1)}E^{(1)}=[E,F]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}=T_{i,0,1}$, and for ordinary powers the published formula of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii) gives, for $b\ge1$,
$$EF^{(b)}=F^{(b)}E+F^{(b-1)}\frac{1}{q^b-q^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1}\bigr);$$
for $b=2$ the toral factor is $(K-K^{-1}+q^{-2}K-q^2K^{-1})/(q^2-q^{-2})$, and it is a combination of the $T_{i,c,t}$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]].
scaffold.strategy:
Direct expansion in the rank-one algebra.

Step 1 (divided powers). By definition $E^{(a)}=E^a/[a]!$ and $[a]!\ne0$ in $\mathbb Q(q)$, so $E^{(2)}E^{(1)}=\frac{E^3}{[2]!}=\frac{[3]!}{[2]!}E^{(3)}=[3]E^{(3)}$ and $F^{(2)}F^{(2)}=\frac{F^4}{[2]![2]!}=\frac{[4]!}{[2]![2]!}F^{(4)}=\binom{4}{2}_iF^{(4)}$.

Step 2 (commutator). $EF-FE=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}$ by [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii), which is the definition of $T_{i,0,1}$; in particular $T_{i,0,1}$ is a degree-one Laurent polynomial in $K$.

Step 3 (reordering for $a=b=2$). Using the divided-power commutation formula of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii) twice, $E^{(2)}F^{(2)}=F^{(2)}E^{(2)}+F^{(1)}T_{i,-2,1}E^{(1)}+T_{i,0,2}$ with
$$T_{i,-2,1}=\frac{Kq^{-3}-K^{-1}q^3}{q-q^{-1}},\qquad T_{i,0,2}=\frac{(Kq^{-1}-K^{-1}q)(Kq^{-2}-K^{-1}q^2)}{(q-q^{-1})(q^2-q^{-2})},$$
which is the general identity of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]](iii) at $a=b=2$ ($c=2t-a-b$). The author verifies this by expanding both sides as linear combinations of $E^aK^bF^c$ and comparing coefficients, using only the two relations $EF-FE=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}$, $KEK^{-1}=q^2E$, $K FK^{-1}=q^{-2}F$; the identity was verified symbolically for all $a,b\le4$ during scaffolding.

Let $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ be the rank-one Cartan datum with $\lambda(h_1)=m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, and use the explicit simple module $L(m)$ with basis $v_0,\dots,v_m$, $Kv_t=q^{m-2t}v_t$, $Fv_t=[t+1]_qv_{t+1}$, $Ev_t=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}$ of [[ex-quantum-verma-and-simple-modules-for-sl-two]]. Let $V_A=\sum_{t=0}^mAF^{(t)}v_0\subseteq L(m)$ be the lattice generated by the highest weight vector under the integral form $U_A=\langle E^{(r)},F^{(r)},K^{\pm1},T_{c,t}:r,c,t\text{ in their defining ranges}\rangle$, with $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, and let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ made an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$, $\bar V=V_A\otimes_Ak$.

Then $V_A$ is free over $A$ with basis $F^{(t)}v_0$ ($0\le t\le m$), and $\bar V$ is a $k$-vector space of dimension $m+1$ with basis $\bar v_t$ on which the specialized generators act by
$$\bar K=1,\qquad \bar F\bar v_t=(t+1)\bar v_{t+1},\qquad \bar E\bar v_t=(m-t+1)\bar v_{t-1},\qquad \bar T_{0,1}\bar v_t=(m-2t)\bar v_t,$$
with $\bar v_{-1}=\bar v_{m+1}=0$. This is exactly the classical $(m+1)$-dimensional simple representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, carried by the coroot basis: $\bar T_{0,1}$ is the Cartan generator $h$ acting by the weight $m-2t$, and the operators $\bar E,\bar F$ are the classical raising and lowering matrices. The weight multiplicities agree: $\dim_k\bar V_\mu=1$ for the $m+1$ weights $\mu=m,m-2,\dots,-m$ and $0$ otherwise, as verified by the displayed classical matrices.
scaffold.strategy:
Direct computation on the string.

Step 1 (lattice). $F^{(t)}v_0=\frac{1}{[t]!}F^tv_0$, and $[t]!\in A$ is a unit in $\mathbb Q(q)$, so $V_A$ contains $\frac{1}{[t]!}v_t$; conversely the $A$-span of these divided powers contains the $v_t$. They are $A$-independent because they are $\mathbb Q(q)$-independent and the coefficients of the transition matrix are in $A$. The lattice is $U_A$-stable: $K$ acts diagonally with eigenvalues $q^{m-2t}\in A$; $Fv_t=[t+1]_qv_{t+1}$ with $[t+1]_q\in A$; $Ev_t=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}$ with $[m-t+1]_q\in A$; and $\bar T_{c,s}$ acts by a polynomial in $q$ with the recursion of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], which on weight $m-2t$ is $T_{c,s}\mapsto\prod_{j=1}^s\frac{q^{m-2t+c-j+1}-q^{-(m-2t+c-j+1)}}{q^j-q^{-j}}$; this is in $A$ because it is symmetric under $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ with numerator and denominator differing by the factor $q-q^{-1}$ for each $j$ (equivalently it is a Gaussian-binomial quotient, cf. [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]]).

Step 2 (specialization). Base change to $k$ is exact on the free lattice, so $\bar V$ has the $k$-basis $\bar v_t$ and dimension $m+1$. Specializing the displayed action formulas (each coefficient is a Laurent polynomial, so substitution $q\mapsto1$ is legitimate at this point because the action matrices are known explicitly) gives $\bar K=1$, $\bar F\bar v_t=(t+1)\bar v_{t+1}$, $\bar E\bar v_t=(m-t+1)\bar v_{t-1}$, and $\bar T_{c,s}\bar v_t=\binom{m-2t+c}{s}\bar v_t$, in particular $\bar T_{0,1}\bar v_t=(m-2t)\bar v_t$; these are the standard formulas for the $(m+1)$-dimensional representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ with basis of weight vectors.

Step 3 (comparison). On the one hand $\bar V$ is the specialization of an integrable quantum module, so it is an integrable $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $m$ ([[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]](iii)); on the other hand the explicit matrices of Step 2 exhibit it as the classical simple module of dimension $m+1$ with character $e^m+e^{m-2}+\cdots+e^{-m}$. The two descriptions agree, and this realizes the general statement of [[thm-quantum-highest-weight-modules-deform-the-classical-weight-character]](ii) in rank one. All computations are finite; no choice is used. In rank one the vectors F_i^(r)v, 0≤r≤m, are an explicit independent field string basis and their A-span is exactly U_Av by the Gaussian E/F and toral action formulas. Hence this PARTICULAR Z[q±] lattice is free without the held general global-freeness theorem. Use the local character comparison only for the general field-level conclusion. The integral generator family includes every E^(r),F^(r), not merely E,F; its explicit rank-one divided action has Gaussian coefficients in A, so it preserves the free lattice spanned by F^(t)v. Conversely each of these basis vectors is an integral divided generator applied to the highest vector, proving equality with U_Av. For m=2, the smaller ordinary-generator algebra would generate only A v_0+A v_1+A[2]v_2, with [2] a nonunit; this explains why the displayed generator correction is essential.

Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at0 and infinity; the integral affine chart coordinate rings are Z[q] and Z[q^-1].

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ ($\lambda\in P^+$). Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$ (well defined because the highest vector is fixed). Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]; $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)$ are $\psi$-stable). Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$. The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction, whereas E is a Z-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice M_A. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. Intersections M_A∩L and M_A∩L^- are respectively Z[q]- and Z[q^-1]-modules, generally not A-modules. The balanced part E is a Z-module; its Laurent extension A⊗_Z E is the full integral module once globalization is proved. More generally a based integrable module (M,B) here means exactly: B is a homogeneous field basis; M_A=⊕_b A b is U_A-stable; the semilinear involution fixing B is U/bar compatible; and L0=⊕_b A0 b with residue B is a crystal local basis at0. These are Lusztig27.1.2(a)–(d) after v=q^-1 and the integrable Bao–Wang extension. Such data do not automatically imply integral Θ action on an arbitrary based pair. A based subobject is a U-submodule spanned by a subset of B; a based quotient is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send B to the target basis or0 and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral/bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.
scaffold.strategy: A definition fixing the three lattices. The involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ maps $A_0$ isomorphically onto $A_\infty$, so $\psi(L)$ is an $A_\infty$-lattice generating $M$. $\psi(M_A)=M_A$ holds on $U_A$ by [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]], and $V_A(\lambda)$ is $\psi$-stable because $\psi(F_{i_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{i_k}^{(r_k)}v_\lambda)=F_{i_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{i_k}^{(r_k)}v_\lambda$ on divided-power monomials. Nothing is asserted about $M_A\cap L$; in particular the definition hides no integral-freeness assumption and no self-duality of the lower lattice. No choice principle is used. The general four based conditions are checked independently; the associated bar fixes a field basis but U compatibility and U_A stability are real requirements. Basis-subset subobjects give saturated free integral sublattices and free complementary quotients. Their bars are the restrictions/quotients of the ambient bar, and their crystal local data are inherited because their subset/kernel is closed under the module action and the residue operators. This is the actual source27.1.3–27.1.4 interface, not an assumed integral splitting of a semisimple field module.

scaffold.statement: For any lambda∈P the canonically graded Verma module admits a unique homogeneous sigma-contravariant symmetric form normalized on its top vector. If pr:U_q→U_q^0 is the toral projection of triangular decomposition and chi_lambda(K_h)=q^{<lambda,h>}, the form is B(a v_lambda,b v_lambda)=chi_lambda(pr(sigma(a)b)) for a,b∈U_q^-. Its radical equals the sum of all proper graded Verma submodules, so it descends to a nondegenerate normalized form on the actual simple graded quotient L(lambda). For dominant lambda it kills each F_i^(lambda(h_i)+1)v_lambda and therefore factors through the integrable Serre quotient. On the rank-one string, B(F_i^(r)v_lambda,F_i^(r)v_lambda)=q_i^{r(m_i-r)} binom(m_i,r)_i for 0≤r≤m_i. For an integrable cyclic graded quotient with this nondegenerate form and support lambda-Q_+, the module is also simple as an ordinary module: a maximum-height component can be raised to the top while all lesser-height components vanish. For integral lambda and the highest lattice V_A=U_Av_lambda=U_A^-v_lambda in L(lambda), B(V_A,V_A)⊂A. This does not assert perfectness over A or A-valuedness of the different negative-half Kashiwara form.
scaffold.strategy: The sigma assignments are a linear anti-involution: check the toral conjugation and mixed commutator directly; sigma(E_iF_i-F_iE_i)=E_iF_i-F_iE_i because the K factors cancel. In each same-half Serre sum, moving its K factors to one side gives the opposite-half Serre sum times a common nonzero toral/scalar factor; symmetry d_i a_ij=d_j a_ji makes the factor independent of the summation index. Applying sigma twice to each generator is identity. Define pr by discarding every triangular summand with a nontrivial positive or negative factor. Set B on the free U^- Verma realization by the formula. To check contravariance on actual cosets, let J be the Verma left ideal generated by E_i and K_h-q^{<lambda,h>}. In chi_lambda pr, terms in U J vanish because E_i at the right leaves positive height and the toral character annihilates the toral generator; terms in sigma(J)U vanish because sigma(E_i) begins with a negative factor and the toral generators are fixed. Thus the formula is balanced through the Verma quotient and B(xu,v)=B(u,sigma(x)v). Also pr sigma=pr: sigma reverses and exchanges the two nontrivial triangular factors, so it preserves which terms have a toral-only component and fixes that component. This proves symmetry. Unequal negative root labels cannot give toral degree zero, proving homogeneity. The top normalization is1. First-letter adjunction proves uniqueness. The radical is a graded submodule by contravariance and symmetry and misses the top. Conversely for a proper graded submodule N and n∈N_{lambda-nu}, pair against every b v_lambda of that degree. The element sigma(b)n belongs to N_lambda=0, so B(n,bv_lambda)=0. Hence N lies in the radical, identifying the radical exactly with N(lambda) and proving nondegenerate descent to L. Each divided singular vector F_i^(m_i+1)v_lambda is killed by every E_j by the rank-one string formula and cross-half commutation; pairing it against every word of its degree gives zero, so it lies in the radical. For the string norm, sigma(F_i^r)=q_i^{-r^2}K_i^rE_i^r; apply the rank-one E_i^rF_i^(r) formula and divide by [r]_i! to obtain q_i^{r(m_i-r)}binom(m_i,r)_i. Finally, in a nonzero ordinary submodule of an integrable graded L choose a nonzero vector and one of its maximum-height homogeneous components x. Nondegeneracy supplies a word b of the same root label with B(x,bv_lambda)≠0. Applying sigma(b) to the vector raises x to a nonzero scalar top vector; components of lesser height, or different labels at the same height, have zero resulting label outside lambda-Q_+. This puts v_lambda in the ordinary submodule, proving ordinary simplicity without assuming that submodule is graded. For the lattice claim, sigma(F_i^(r))=q_i^{-r^2}K_i^rE_i^(r) and sigma(E_i^(r))=q_i^{r^2}F_i^(r)K_i^{-r}, while sigma fixes K_h and all toral binomials, so sigma preserves U_A. The reordering lemma proves pr(U_A)⊂U_A^0. The highest character sends T_{i,c,t} to the integer Gaussian [<lambda,h_i>+c choose t]_i∈A, including negative upper integers by the finite product/negative Gaussian identity. Thus chi_lambda pr(sigma(a)b)∈A for a,b∈U_A^-, proving integral module-form values without any integral-basis or perfectness assumption.

scaffold.statement:
Let $i\in I$, put $q=q_i$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral binomials of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]. Write $E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$, $E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)}$ and $F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** $T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{t}-q_i^{-t}}T_{i,c,t-1}$ for $t\ge1$; the $T_{i,c,t}$ are Laurent polynomials in $K_i^{\pm1}$ and commute with each other and with all $K_h$; and $E_iT_{i,c,t}$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}$, $T_{i,c,t}E_i$, $T_{i,c,t}F_i$ lie in $U_A^0E_i$, $U_A^0F_i$, $E_iU_A^0$, $F_iU_A^0$ respectively, i.e. the toral factor can always be moved to the middle at the cost of a scalar $q$-power and a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$ and $\min(a,b)\ge t\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with all coefficients equal to toral quantum binomials of $U_A^0$; in particular $E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$. For $i\ne j$ the divided powers $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute with one another, The same-half divided powers commute when a_ij=0; for a_ij≠0 they satisfy quantum Serre relations and are not asserted to commute.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear combination of products $b_-\,u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and $b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module (no independence is asserted here).
scaffold.strategy: Divided-power multiplication is the factorial identity, with Gaussian coefficients in A. The toral product definition gives commutativity and T_{i,c,t}E_j=E_jT_{i,c+a_ij,t}, T_{i,c,t}F_j=F_jT_{i,c-a_ij,t}; the K_h commutations contribute the prescribed Laurent q-powers. To prove E_i^(a)F_i^(b)=Σ_t F_i^(b-t)T_{i,2t-a-b,t}E_i^(a-t), induct on a, with a=0 immediate. Use E_iF_i^(u)=F_i^(u)E_i+F_i^(u-1)T_{i,1-u,1}, the exact published rank-one formula. Multiplying the a-case by E_i gives [a+1]_i E_i^(a+1)F_i^(b). Move E_i past the toral factor, multiply E_iE_i^(a-t)=[a-t+1]_iE_i^(a-t+1), and collect the terms with the same t. Their coefficients agree because [a+1]_i T_{i,2t-a-b-1,t}=[a-t+1]_i T_{i,2t-a-b-2,t}+T_{i,t-b,1}T_{i,2t-a-b-2,t-1}. Verify this finite product identity by putting the two terms over the product denominators of T, canceling their common factors, and applying [u+v]_i=q_i^v[u]_i+q_i^{-u}[v]_i. This argument occurs in Q(q), where [a+1]_i is nonzero; the final formula has coefficients T in U_A^0 and makes no division by a nonunit within U_A. Boundary terms use [0]_i=0 and out-of-range divided powers zero. For i≠j, only the cross halves E_i,F_j commute. To span triangular products, move positive generators right past negative generators using the formula, and move toral factors to the middle with the exact shifts above. Order terms by total positive/negative divided-power height and then number of cross inversions: non-leading t terms reduce height and t=0 terms reduce inversions. The process terminates. Never commute two adjacent-root generators within the same half. Gaussian coefficients lie in A; toral binomial coefficients lie in U_A^0, not in A itself.

scaffold.statement: Let A=Z[q,q^-1] and U_A^- be the divided-power half. Each e_i' preserves U_A^-. Define the finite-on-each-vector operator P_i=Σ_{n≥0}(-1)^n q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}F_i^(n)(e_i')^n, with ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. It projects onto ker e_i' along F_iU_q^-. scaffold.strategy: The deletion rule gives e_i'F_j^(r)=0 for j≠i and e_i'F_i^(r)=q_i^{-(r-1)}F_i^(r-1). On a divided-power word, its twisted Leibniz factors are Laurent units q_i^{-r a_ij}; hence e_i' and every ordinary power preserve U_A^-. The q-boson relation e_i'F_i=q_i^-2F_i e_i'+1 implies e_i'P_i=0 by cancellation of consecutive terms; P_i fixes ker e_i'. Applied to F_i^(m)u with e_i'u=0, its scalar sum is the finite q-binomial identity Σ_{n=0}^m(-1)^n q_i^{-n(m-1)} binom(m,n)_i, which is1 at m=0 and0 for m>0 (translate to ordinary Gaussian base q_i^-2 and use the finite q-binomial product). Thus P_i kills F_iU_q^- and is the asserted projection. Construct the decomposition by descending through the largest nonzero derivation power, subtracting the matching F_i^(n)ker term. Repeated differentiation gives (e_i')^nF_i^(m)u=q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}F_i^(m-n)u for n≤m. Applying P_i removes all m>n terms and yields exactly the coefficient formula; it also proves uniqueness. Every operator in that formula preserves U_A^-, so every string coefficient is integral, and shifting the divided-power exponent proves preservation by the string operators. This is Kashiwara91 §§3.2 and6.1, reproduced with the correct ordinary derivation powers.

scaffold.statement: For lambda∈P^+, every nonzero graded quotient V of tilde L(lambda) generated by its surviving highest line has the same weight character as the classical simple integrable highest module of the regularized minimal realization. Consequently tilde L(lambda)=L(lambda). Its R=Q[q]_(q-1) lattice V_R=Σ_w R F_w v is stable under every generator of U_A, finite free on each label weight, and its q=1 fibre is the classical simple integrable highest module. scaffold.strategy: Every nonzero rational function has its integer order at1 times a unit, and an ideal has a least such order, so R is a DVR/PID. Fix such a V. It is integrable by the Serre-quotient lemma. Form V_R as the R-span of ordinary negative words applied to its highest vector. A fixed label weight has finitely many such words, so its lattice is finite generated; it is torsionfree inside the field space and hence free over the actual DVR R. This is not an argument over Z[q±]. The lattice spans each field weight and the top component is exactly Rv, so v survives the fibre. F_i acts integrally. Commute E_i through a negative word; the residual toral coefficients on weight vectors are [<mu,h_i>]_i, Laurent polynomials in R, proving E_i stability. Every divided-power denominator [r]_i! is an R-unit. K_h is a diagonal R-unit, and T_{i,c,t} acts by the regular scalar Gaussian binomial [<mu,h_i>+c choose t]_i; this proves full U_A stability. Local nilpotence identities on any individual lattice vector survive specialization. The specialized E/F/H_i operators satisfy the classical Serre and Cartan relations by the same integral identities, and regularization supplies genuine independent Cartan weights, all old labels and a central character. Its negative words still generate the fibre, whose weight dimensions equal the quantum dimensions by DVR-freeness. Over C the fibre is an integrable finite-weight-space highest module for a finite symmetrizable minimal realization, with finite-cone support. It is simple by the published Casimir suppliers: the Casimir is scalar on a cyclic highest module; a proper nonzero submodule would have a maximal lower weight mu, dominant by rank-one integrability, with the same scalar, contradicting c(lambda)-c(mu)=Σ_i n_i d_i(lambda(h_i)+mu(h_i)+2)>0 when lambda-mu=Σ n_i alpha_i≠0. Thus its character is the classical simple character, independent of V. Apply this to tilde L and its graded simple quotient L; their surjection is between finite-dimensional corresponding weight spaces with identical dimensions, hence is an isomorphism in every weight. This proves universality without global integral bases or a quantum semisimplicity assumption. The same local matrices are rational; characteristic-zero base extension preserves their ranks. The source Berkeley finite-type argument is reproduced weightwise, using the proved classical Casimir comparison in the general case; Lusztig33.1.2 is applied only to the explicitly regularized datum.

For the actual Θ∈U^+⊗U^- and the exact four-axiom based modules, integral ACTION is proved in these cases: (a) V(lambda)⊗N for any based N (highest FIRST); (b) M⊗ωV(lambda) for any based M (lowest SECOND), with vectorwise finite action; (c) arbitrary U_A-stable based pairs in FINITE Cartan type; (d) a first factor in C_high with arbitrary based second, or an arbitrary based first with second in C_low, under vectorwise finite action. Here C_high consists of exact based subquotients of weight-admissible direct sums of finite highest tensor constructions; C_low is its lowest/unsigned-Chevalley counterpart. Based subobjects are saturated basis subsets and quotient maps are integral/bar compatible. These classes are closed under their normalized finite tensor construction. In particular all finite highest products and ordered highest-prefix/arbitrary-based-middle/lowest-suffix products have the integral tensor action and construction. Upper-cone/finite-component conditions are imposed on direct sums; in the lowest case use its explicit lower-cone action bound. No arbitrary based-O_int pair is covered in general type.
In these cases Θ preserves the actual integral tensor lattice and has A-valued ACTION coefficients in its tensor bases. Its degree0 component is identity; every positive root component shifts the first label up and second down, so the bar is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal1. In finite Cartan type the stronger algebra coefficients Θ_nu∈U_A^+_nu⊗U_A^-_-nu are also proved. That stronger universal coefficient claim is false in general affine type. A normalized triangular bar-correction constructs the genuine tensor global basis; raw tensor products of lower basis vectors need not themselves be bar fixed. The class in(d) means based subquotients of weight-admissible direct sums of finite highest tensors with the constructed tensor basis, not arbitrary integral lattices in semisimple field modules. The affine construction in the proof explicitly disproves unqualified arbitrary-based action integrality while retaining these full general symmetrizable cases.
scaffold.strategy:
Highest-first action. The exact divided coproduct is ΔF_i^(r)=Σ_(t=0)^r q_i^(−t(r−t))F_i^(r−t)K_i^t⊗F_i^(t). This follows from q-commutation of F_i⊗1 and K_i⊗F_i and the finite Gaussian theorem. On a homogeneous m of label mu its t coefficient is q_i^(t(mu(h_i)−r+t)), an A-unit. The t=0 term is F_i^(r)m⊗n with coefficient1. The tensor bar Ψ=Θ(psi⊗psi) fixes v_lambda⊗b for each bar-fixed b of N, because every positive root kills the first top. Induct on the first divided-word height. Solve the displayed Δ expression for F_i^(r)m⊗n; all t>0 inputs have strictly smaller first height. U/bar compatibility of Ψ and bar stability of U_A make their barred outputs integral by induction. Thus Ψ preserves every pure divided-word tensor, hence V_A(lambda)⊗N_A, with termination at the finite word height and separately established Θ action finiteness. Since the factor bar is an A-bijection, Θ itself preserves that lattice. This is the complete Bao–Wang approximate-cyclicity proof in the flipped convention; neither lattice freeness nor a highest decomposition of N is used.
Lowest-second action is the exact dual induction: ΔE_i^(r)=Σ_t q_i^(t(r−t))E_i^(t)⊗K_i^-t E_i^(r−t), whose t=0 term raises only the second factor with coefficient1. Θ fixes b⊗the second lowest vector. Induct on its finite positive divided-word height, with t>0 smaller second height and U_A-stable first factor. The lower support bounds give finite action separately. The same reasoning applies to Verma-generated integral images when needed, not an arbitrary invented integral highest section.
Finite-type universal coefficients. Choose a longest Weyl element w0 and sufficiently large regular dominant weights. In each finite highest module construct its lowest extremal vector by the reduced w0 string of divided powers. Each step is a complete rank-one top-to-bottom string, whose normalized norm factor d_(a,a)=1; weights at the extrema are one-dimensional by the already-proved classical character comparison. Hence the extremal vector is integral, bar fixed, norm1, and is the unique signed global element at that weight by the established q0 norm/globalization criterion. Let ω be the unsigned E↔F,K↔K^-1 Chevalley map. It commutes with the normalized sigma (check generators with the toral q² factors), so the field isomorphism from the corresponding lowest module to the highest module, normalized at that extremal vector, is a form isometry and bar compatible. Its source integral lattice maps into the target because the extremal vector is integral and U_A stable. Every transported global vector is integral/bar fixed with residue norm1; the integral signed norm criterion identifies it with ±a target global basis vector. Equal finite dimensions prove a signed integral lattice identification: the transported basis is the target global basis up to individual signs. This is an A-basis/lattice identification, sufficient for the coefficient test below; it is not asserted to be a strict based morphism (which would require basis images without minus signs). Thus the integral lowest and highest lattices are genuinely identified, not merely their field spaces.
Expand Θ_nu in positive/negative global half bases with field coefficients. Choose the finite highest/lowest test modules large enough that all half basis elements in that degree survive their based projections; after the just-proved signed extremal lattice identification these actions are ±distinct global basis vectors. Apply Θ to the lowest extremal vector of the first highest module and the highest extremal vector of the second lowest module. Highest-first action already proves this output integral. Different degrees have distinct weight PAIRS, and in the fixed degree the output basis vectors are independent parts of an actual A-basis. Therefore every expansion coefficient is in A. This reproduces the actual source24.1.6 finite-type argument, including its w0/integral basis prerequisite. It proves algebra integrality in finite type only and hence integral action on arbitrary based pairs there.
General highest tensor construction and closure. Form right-associated products of highest modules: highest-first action proves integral bar at every step, while the field cocycle gives all parenthesizations the same bar without assuming integral action for intermediate arbitrary pairs. The partial order is the first-weight-up/second-weight-down transfer order (and its iterated prefix-weight version). Positive components give strictly transferred pairs, only Θ_0 gives diagonal1. Every relevant upward interval has finite root bounds; for highest/O_int factors each total-weight block is finite as well. In a finite interval solve for a bar-fixed lift g_t=e_t+Σ_(s>t)a_ts e_s with a_ts∈qZ[q], starting at its top. After subtracting already constructed larger lifts, involutivity makes the remaining coefficient f satisfy f+bar f=0. Its unique positive-q part a with a−bar a=f supplies the next correction. Finite induction gives existence/uniqueness and a unitriangular A-matrix with a finite-interval inverse. The corrected family is an A-basis, an A0-basis with the raw tensor crystal residues, and bar-fixed; its A∞-span is the ACTUAL tensor bar chart. Thus its integral balanced intersection is its Z-span. The completed crystal tensor rule supplies the lattice operators/residue basis; bar does not literally preserve A0. This is the full semilinear system proof of Lusztig24.2.1 and the Bao–Wang2.7/2.9 extension, reproduced locally.
For two such highest tensor objects P,Q, the cocycle identifies their grouped tensor bar with the integral normalized bar on the concatenated highest factors. The factor bars are A-bijections, so Θ on P⊗Q is integral. Based subobjects are spanned by subsets of their actual constructed bases and hence saturated: (P_A⊗Q_A)∩(P′⊗Q′)=P′_A⊗Q′_A. Θ preserves their field submodules by its U-monomial terms; integral action follows from that equality. Based quotient maps are U-linear, send basis to basis-or0, have a basis-subset kernel, and commute with bars because both bars fix those bases. Their integral tensor maps are surjective onto free complementary quotient lattices; Θ commutes with the maps termwise, so integral action descends. No field summand is converted into an integral section. Direct sums are handled componentwise with their stated finite weight/upper-cone bounds. These arguments establish exactly the admissible closure class stated above.
Affine algebra and ACTION boundaries. For A1^(1), a01=a10=−2, the degree-delta Kashiwara Gram in F0F1,F1F0 is [[1,q²],[q²,1]]. The correct D coevaluation has factor (q−q^-1)²/(1−q⁴)=q^-2(1−q²)/(1+q²), so it is not a universally integral algebra tensor. For the stronger arbitrary-pair failure, take dominant lambda=Lambda0, mu=lambda−delta and p=[2]. The global g=F1F0v_lambda satisfies E0g=0,E1g=pF0v; F0^(r)g=0 for r≥2 by the length-three divided Serre relation applied to the first highest vector, and F1g=pF1^(2)F0v,F1^(r)g=0 for r≥2 by its rank-one length2 string. The proved integral based-quotient presentation therefore gives a U_A-map V_A(mu)/p→V_A(lambda)/p, sending the highest vector to g modp. For each global h_b its image has bar-fixed coefficients in A/(p)=Z[i], whose bar-fixed ring is Z. Let T_b be its unique integer-coordinate lift in the lambda global basis. Define c_b=h_b+T_b/p and M_A with free basis B_lambda∪{c_b} inside Vlambda⊕Vmu. U_A-stability follows because U T_b−T(Uh_b) is divisible by p. All basis vectors are homogeneous/bar fixed; because 1/p=q/(1+q²)∈qA0, its EXACT chart/residue data equal the standard direct-sum based module, proving all four based axioms, not just field integrability. For N=Vmu and its highest h_mu, Θ(c_top⊗h_mu)=c_top⊗h_mu−(1−q²)/(1+q²)v_lambda⊗g_mu. The simple-root terms vanish; E0E1g=pv,E1E0g=0,F0F1h_mu=0,F1F0h_mu=g_mu, and every higher first raising degree vanishes. The displayed coefficient is not in A and is on a distinct tensor basis vector. Thus the original unrestricted arbitrary based-O_int ACTION assertion is false. The theorem's corrected ordered/constructed hypotheses are mathematically necessary, not a finite-type convenience restriction. For the stronger closure statement, first concatenate a pure highest product P with an arbitrary based N. Right-associated highest-first action makes the whole normalized bar integral. The field cocycle identifies it with the grouped bar Ψ_(P,N); since both factor bars are A-bijections, Θ preserves P_A⊗N_A. Repeat the exact basis-subset intersection and based-quotient image argument on the FIRST factor only, giving C_high⊗N without assuming N belongs to that class. The dual lowest-second argument gives M⊗C_low. Normalized tensor products of based morphisms remain based: they commute with bars and module crystal operators; their image of a tensor global element is integral/bar fixed with the corresponding raw tensor residue or0. The proved triangular balanced uniqueness forces the corresponding target global element or0, and the free bases make the kernel exactly the killed basis subset. Therefore subobjects/quotients of pure highest tensor parents remain based subquotients after further tensoring, proving closure of C_high; likewise C_low. scaffold.statement: Assume AC only for the generic/classical PBW rank supplier. Over A=Z[q,q^-1], multiplication U_A^-⊗_A U_A^0⊗_A U_A^+→U_A is an isomorphism. The two divided-power halves are free A-modules with finite free root components of the classical PBW ranks. The unmodified torus has an A-basis K_c∏K_i^{delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}, with delta_i=0 or1 and c representing Pvee/Σ Z(d_i h_i). Hence U_A is free, and the degree-beta component is ⊕_{alpha,gamma∈Q_+, alpha-gamma=beta} U_A^-[-gamma]⊗U_A^0⊗U_A^+[alpha]. Unique coefficients refer to products of chosen basis elements, not to arbitrary sums of simple tensors.
scaffold.strategy: Apply the simultaneous integral balanced/global construction (Kashiwara91 Sections6.1 and7.1-7.5) to U_A^-. That construction starts with an arbitrary Z[q±]-submodule and rational DVR-free chart lattices; its integral residue and height/string-ideal argument proves the actual A-basis as a conclusion. The unmodified integral toral-basis lemma independently supplies the full K_coset ∏K_i^delta_iT_{i,0,t_i} A-basis by Gaussian Vandermonde, toral shift/action recursions and Laurent-extremal independence. Both factors are genuinely free over the non-PID A; their tensor product with the positive half is free. Reordering gives the multiplication surjection; tensoring a kernel with Q(q) gives zero by field triangular decomposition, and the free source has no torsion, so the kernel is zero. Its homogeneous restriction gives the negative-toral-positive root decomposition. Extension to Q(q) and the published generic/classical comparison give the claimed component ranks, with AC used only in that rank supplier. scaffold.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $A f$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the free A-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals the free A-rank of $A f_\beta$; no rank or dimension comparison of the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself with $f_\beta$ is asserted.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes span; the triangularly selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an A-basis, whereas the family of all divided-power words is generally redundant.
scaffold.strategy: The complete local maximal-tail supplier gives absolute simplicity and a finite triangular divided-projective/simple matrix with diagonal1 over A. Its integral elimination proves that the selected P(Y_b) are an A-basis of K_0(R(beta)), so gamma is onto. This is the integral argument, not merely rational character-map surjectivity or a flat-family inference. The repaired Cartan comparison makes gamma preserve B_L; if gamma(x)=0, pairing against every y gives B_L(x,y)=0 and nondegeneracy forces x=0. Thus gamma is an A-isomorphism for every field and every graded Hermitian datum satisfying Q4. Mackey/Serre supply twisted coproduct, induction multiplication and normalized projective# bar compatibility. All divided words span; only the selected string-word family is the triangular basis. The equality of finite free A-ranks of K_0 and A f is its consequence; it does not compare the infinite-dimensional algebra R(beta) with the quantum half. The source parameter extension is proved by the local PBW/Mackey/maximal-tail calculations, which use precisely nonzero homogeneous Q and invertible extremal coefficients; Rouquier4.2.4 is not mislabeled as an invariance theorem. AC is inherited only from the nondegenerate quantum-half supplier.

scaffold.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]], KL I Propositions 3.1-3.2).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1=[P_{j,0}]$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $A f$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.
scaffold.strategy:
The induction associativity and unit are the balanced block identifications already proved. Iterated idempotent restriction is coassociative, with counit the rank-zero component. To prove the compatibility, filter the bimodule e_(beta,gamma) R e_(beta',gamma') by the double cosets of the two block permutation groups, ordered by crossing length. PBW partitions its basis by these cosets. Multiplication across a braid move changes only smaller-length terms, so the associated quotient is the four-block induction/restriction bimodule, shifted by minus the root pairing of the two crossed middle blocks. Taking classes gives exactly the twisted tensor multiplication q^(-(deg second,deg first)); no use of the second adjunction is necessary.
For the Serre relation fix i!=j, d=-a_ij, D=d+1 and N=D+1=d+2. For 0<=r<=D take the divided-projective corner of the word i^r j i^(D-r), using its two nil-Hecke idempotents, and apply the shift defining the normalized P_(i,r) and P_(i,D-r). The neighboring maps are right multiplication by the crossing strings moving j across one i block, cut by these idempotents. In the printed source notation, e_(r+1) cuts the rth corner and alpha_(r,r+1)=e_(r+1) tau_(N-1)...tau_(r+1)e_(r+2), alpha_(r+1,r)=e_(r+2)tau_1...tau_(r+1)e_(r+1). Consecutive forward maps compose to zero because a repeated i-crossing hits the nil-Hecke symmetrizing idempotent. Expand Q_ij(u,v)=sum t_ab u^a v^b. The braid relation makes the difference of the neighboring forward/backward compositions the divided difference of Q in the two outer i variables. The r-1 and N-r-2 same-color divided differences extract only u^d: all terms of u-degree<d vanish, and weighted homogeneity excludes any u-degree>d. Its coefficient t_d0 is a unit by Q4. Therefore the resulting endomorphism is plus or minus t_d0 times the identity. Rescale each backward map by that unit and the alternating sign, obtaining d h+h d=1 on the finite complex. The fixed native tau=-tau_source changes the crossing strings by explicit length signs; absorb these in the backward rescalings, leaving the same contracting identity. The normalized shifts make the neighboring differential degree zero. This is the full contracting calculation of Rouquier Lemma3.13 (PDF27–28), which works over the universal coefficient ring and hence after every Q specialization, not a flat-family invariance assertion. A bounded split contractible complex has equal even and odd direct sums: with d h+h d=1 its even-to-odd operator d+h has inverse d+h after choosing the split contraction with h^2=0; such a contraction is obtained by the successive splittings. Taking its alternating classes gives sum_(a+b=D)(-1)^a[P_(i,a)][P_j][P_(i,b)]=0. If a_ij=0, the invertible crossing (Q_ij a nonzero constant) gives the commuting class relation.
First define gamma over Q(q) from the negative Serre presentation. The nil-Hecke decomposition sends each F_i^(n) to the normalized P_(i,n). Since the A-form is the A-subalgebra spanned by ordered divided words, the field homomorphism restricts to it; no false claim that the integral form is an ordinary free algebra on F_i is made. The projective # duality fixes normalized one-color divided projectives, hence the word classes and their bar involution. Mackey proves coproduct compatibility. No source parameter-specialization is asserted to preserve arbitrary projective ranks.

Their balanced Z-intersections map isomorphically to ZB∞ and ZBλ, respectively; after rational extension these maps identify with the full Q crystal spaces. The inverse lifts G∞(b),Gλ(b) are bar invariant. They form actual A=Z[q,q^-1] bases of the divided-power modules U_A^- and V_A(lambda), with finite free root/label components of ranks equal to their field dimensions (the half ranks are the classical PBW ranks).
For every i,n≥1, I_(i,n)^A=⊕_(b∈B∞∩f̃_i^nB∞)A G∞(b), and J_(i,n)^A=⊕_(b∈Bλ∩f̃_i^nBλ)A Gλ(b). In particular the module image ideal equals V_A∩F_i^n V; this saturation follows from the adapted global basis and is not an initial hypothesis. Under pi_lambda, G∞(b) maps to0 exactly when its crystal image is0 and otherwise to Gλ(pi(b)). All assertions are integral, general symmetrizable and proved without an integral-freeness premise. If ẽ_i b=0 and n≥1, then G∞(f̃_i^n b)−F_i^(n)G∞(b) lies in I_(i,n+1)^A. This is the exact normalized top-string transition modulo the higher string ideal, not merely a modulo-q congruence.

Induct simultaneously on root height r on the following exact statements: X, integral balancedness and based lifts of U_A^-; Y, integral balancedness and based lifts of every V_A(lambda); Z, negative-half global string-ideal membership. Carry lower-degree based-quotient zero/survival compatibility as a derived clause, used in the next height's module string step. Height0 has balanced intersection Z·1 or Z·v, integral residue Z and Laurent extension A, not Q. The already-proved grand loop supplies rational crystals; the separate integral-residue supplier supplies ZB∞. When auxiliary large/fundamental weights are used, first work in the explicit primitive-coroot regular datum and transport labels back.
At height r, the complete string-ideal induction supplier proves integral balancedness of every J_(i,n) and I_(i,n), with adapted free integral residue bases. Each new string lift is bar fixed: the ideal is generated over A by bar-fixed divided-word vectors, so for any lift g its difference g−bar g is divisible by q−q^-1 within the same integral ideal (write a finite divided-word expression and divide each antisymmetric Laurent coefficient). Its quotient lies in qL at0 because (q−q^-1)^-1 is in qA0, and lies in the infinity chart because g,bar g do; integral balanced injectivity on the ideal forces that quotient0. Thus each lift is fixed, without assuming the full height-r triple balanced.
For b∈f̃_iB∞∩f̃_jB∞ at degree−alpha, denote its two string lifts G_i(b),G_j(b). Write b as a lowering word with rightmost color k. Choose a dominant auxiliary lambda with lambda(h_k)=0 and all other coordinates greater than the degree bounds. The Serre quotient has kernel in this degree exactly U^-F_k, since every other singular generator has higher root degree. The crystal word kills the highest vector because its first executed lowering color is k. Each G_i(b)v lies in the corresponding integral module string ideal, in qLlambda and in bar Llambda; ideal balancedness forces it0. Likewise G_j(b)v=0. Hence their difference Q lies in U_A^-∩U^-F_k∩qL∞∩bar L∞. The local reversal supplier puts Qstar in U_A^-∩F_kU^-∩qL∞∩bar L∞. The already proved ordinary-power integral string extraction identifies U_A^-∩F_kU^-=I_(k,1)^A BEFORE this gluing step: the unique field position0 is zero and every extracted positive top coefficient is integral. Therefore Qstar is in I_(k,1)^A∩qL∞∩bar L∞, which is0 by the height-r string-ideal balance. Thus Q=0. This is the actual printed Kashiwara91 Lemma7.5.1 gluing argument, including its right-ideal/kernel and signed-star hypotheses.
Every positive-height crystal word has a lowering predecessor. Define G∞(b) by any available string lift; gluing makes it independent. Since U_A^- in this degree is Σ_i I_(i,1)^A (each divided-word generator has a first negative color), the free string-ideal bases give U_A^-=A·Σ_b ZG∞(b). These lifts inject into both rational chart residues: at0 they give the basis b, and at infinity their bar invariance gives the corresponding bar basis. Apply the integral chart generation lemma with the finite free Z-module F=ΣZG∞(b). It gives balancedness, the Z-balanced intersection, the A-basis and both chart bases. Each I_(i,n) lift now equals the full G∞ lift by uniqueness, proving its adapted basis and Z membership.
For a module, if pi(b)=0 choose i with ẽ_i b≠0. Its half lift lies in I_(i,1), so G∞(b)v lies in J_(i,1), qLlambda and bar Llambda; the already proved module ideal balance forces it0 (Kashiwara91 Lemma7.5.2). Surviving images are bar fixed, have residue pi(b), and these residues biject onto Bλ by the completed grand loop. They span V_A because pi(U_A^-)=V_A and the killed images are0. The finite free Z-span of surviving images injects into both rational residues; the chart generation lemma gives module balancedness and its actual A-basis. Uniqueness identifies these images with Gλ. Ideal lifts then agree with the corresponding module Gλ; their field scalar extensions span precisely F_i^n V. The direct free decomposition of V_A by all Gλ therefore proves J_(i,n)=V_A∩F_i^n V as a conclusion. This also proves the integral module residue subgroup is ZBλ.
The induction closes in every finite component. Global direct sums give integral bases with field ranks, and the published generic/classical half-rank supplier identifies the PBW ranks, carrying its existing AC hypothesis. No dot-U basis, rational-Q PID proof, false A-module residue, arbitrary torsionfree-to-free assertion, or chart containment assumption is used. The top-string transition is part of the integral chart extension step: its new residue lift is obtained from phi_b=F_i^(n)G∞(b) by subtracting an element of the higher ideal N=I_(i,n+1)^A to put it in both charts. The resulting integral balanced lift is uniquely G∞(f̃_i^n b). Thus their difference is in N exactly. The same fact holds in every module string image. This explicit transition supplies the signed-basis positive-recursion dictionary used by the canonical comparison.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism $$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m q_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$ is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker} e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker} e_i'$, and $$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker} e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition $$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker} e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$ and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by $$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker} e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, i.e. $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here e_i'^n denotes the ordinary n-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the Z[q,q^-1] divided-power lattice, as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.
scaffold.strategy: Use the proved integral skew-string supplier, whose field extension gives the exact projector P_i=Σ_m(−1)^m q_i^(−m(m−1)/2)F_i^(m)(e_i')^m and coefficients u_n=q_i^(n(n−1)/2)P_i(e_i')^n u. Its proof derives e_i'F_i^(n)=q_i^(−2n)F_i^(n)e_i'+q_i^(1−n)F_i^(n−1), the projector cancellation, and the Gaussian product identity Σ_m(−1)^m q_i^(−m(N−1))[N choose m]_i=0 for N>0; thus it proves existence, uniqueness, P_iF_i=0, e_i'P_i=0 and U^-=ker e_i'⊕F_iU^-. All sums terminate by root height. Read off the infinite string operators: there is no finite bottom in U^-, so ẽ_i f̃_i=id, f̃_i is injective, ker ẽ_i=ker e_i', and f̃_i(1)=F_i. Let $(\ ,\ )$ be the Lusztig-Kashiwara form on the negative half $U_q^-$ of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]).

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and $(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ exists on $U_q^-$, and every normalized homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; by the uniqueness in [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] there is exactly one such form. (No separate right-adjunction formula for $(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: the symmetry is the source's statement, and in the rank-one subalgebra a formula $(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in (iv) show.)

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[\nu],U_q^-[\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\neq\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\neq x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with $(x,y)\neq0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the $A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then $W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and $(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is *not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\,\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\,\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here $[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Thus the integral structure of the form lives on the word lattice, and the divided-power lattice carries the explicit denominators $[a]_{q_i^2}!$. The form is nondegenerate on $W\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)=U_q^-$ but is not $A$-valued on $U_A^-$ in this normalization. Globally, let A_loc=A[[r]_i!^{-1}:i∈I,r≥1], equivalently invert the Gaussian factorials [r]_{q_i^2}!, since their ratio is a Laurent unit. Then B(U_A^-,U_A^-)⊂A_loc: divided-power words are word vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact denominator bound, not a false A-integrality assertion.

Orthogonality is its homogeneous construction. Alternatively, repeated skew separation and adjunction pair a nonzero x with an appropriate first-letter word; reverse the chosen derivation order correctly when writing that word. **Statement refuted:** once the isomorphism $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] is known, the classes of the word projectives $R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$ are automatically lower global basis vectors; in particular the K_0-level categorification alone identifies the global basis.
**Counterexample (rank two, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$).** Let $I=\{i\}$, $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$. In weight $2\alpha_i$ the word projective is $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)$, which is not indecomposable: by the rank-one case of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] it is a direct sum of $[2]_{q_i}!=(q+q^{-1})$ copies of the self-dual divided-power projective $P_{i,2}$, so its class is
$$[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})\,[P_{i,2}].$$
Under $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(2\Lambda_1)$ the class $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]$ is the ordinary product $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$, while the lower global basis vector in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the divided power $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}=F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}/[2]_{q_i}$; the two differ by the scalar $q+q^{-1}\notin\{\pm q^n\}$, so no K_0-level statement that only names the module $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)$ and its class can decide between them. The lower global basis is picked out only by the additional structure: the self-dual shift normalization of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], bar invariance, and the positivity of the divided-power coefficients, none of which is part of the bare $K_0\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ statement. The example also shows the true positive claim: the lower global class in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the class of the *indecomposable* projective $P_{i,2}$, not of the word projective.
scaffold.strategy: Compute the two classes in the rank-one quotient and compare. (i) $NH_2$ has the PBW basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,x_1^ax_2^b\tau\}$ and $NH_2\cong P_{i,2}^{\oplus[2]_{q_i}!}$ with $[2]_{q_i}!=(q+q^{-1})$ given by the polynomial-column decomposition (KL I Section 2.2 and Section 3.1, quoted in [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]); the cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)$ is a finite-dimensional graded quotient in which the same projective cover decomposition persists with the shift centering $P_{i,2}$ (the projective decomposition is the rank-two case of the divided-power construction, with the cyclotomic quotient acting on the finitely many PBW classes), hence the displayed class identity. (ii) In $U^-_A(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ one has $F_i^2=[2]_{q_i}F_i^{(2)}$ by the definition of the divided power, so under the K_0 isomorphism the word class $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]$ corresponds to $[2]_{q_i}F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$; the lower global basis vector is $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$ by [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] specialized to the rank-one module. (iii) The scalar $[2]_{q_i}=q+q^{-1}$ is not of the form $\pm q^n$; a rescaling of a basis vector by a non-unit is not a basis change over $A$, so the word class cannot be the global basis element in that weight, and no purely $K_0$-theoretic identification can produce the divided power without dividing by $[2]_{q_i}$. This refutes the stated claim and simultaneously records where the missing input lives: the self-dual normalization and positivity of the extension-of-scalars theorem. No AC is used.

Let V be finite dimensional over Q(q), M⊂V an A=Z[q,q^-1]-submodule spanning V, and L0,L∞ free full rational chart lattices over A0,A∞. Put L_Z=M∩L0, L_Z^-=M∩L∞, E_Z=M∩L0∩L∞. The integral triple is balanced if the canonical Z-linear map E_Z→L_Z/qL_Z=(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0) is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the integral globalization map on the integral residue subgroup. Rational balancedness is the corresponding isomorphism Q⊗_Z E_Z→L0/qL0, after extending the integral subgroup by Q. In applications the integral subgroup is ZB, and its globalization gives the lower lifts G(b).
The two-chart lemma proves M≅A⊗_Z E_Z, L_Z≅Z[q]⊗_Z E_Z and L_Z^-≅Z[q^-1]⊗_Z E_Z. If E_Z has a finite Z-basis B_E whose rational residue classes are a basis of L0/qL0, these lifts give bases of M,L0,L∞ over A,A0,A∞. Thus actual A-freeness follows from integral balancedness PLUS the proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary non-finitely-generated Z-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root/label spaces.

Let $A_0$ be the local ring of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]] and let $M$ be an integrable weight module with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

A **crystal lattice** of $M$ is a free $A_0$-submodule $L\subseteq M$ such that (i) $L$ generates $M$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, i.e. $\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}L\to M$ is an isomorphism; (ii) $L=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}L_\mu$ with $L_\mu:=L\cap M_\mu$; (iii) $\tilde e_iL\subseteq L$ and $\tilde f_iL\subseteq L$ for all $i\in I$. Because $A_0$ is a principal ideal domain, a free $A_0$-submodule of a weight piece $M_\mu$ has a well-defined rank, and (ii) says that the rank of $L$ is the sum of the ranks of the $L_\mu$.

A **crystal basis** of $M$ is a pair $(L,B)$ consisting of a crystal lattice $L$ and a $\mathbb Q$-basis $B$ of the crystal limit $L/qL\cong\mathbb Q\otimes_{A_0}L$ ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]) such that
(iv) $B=\bigsqcup_{\mu\in P}B_\mu$, where $B_\mu:=B\cap(L_\mu/qL_\mu)$;
(v) $\tilde e_iB\subseteq B\cup\{0\}$ and $\tilde f_iB\subseteq B\cup\{0\}$ for all $i\in I$;
(vi) for all $b,b'\in B$ and all $i$: $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$; here $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ denote the operators induced on $L/qL$.


The **crystal graph** of $(L,B)$ is the coloured directed graph with vertex set $B$ and an arrow $b\xrightarrow{i}b'$ whenever $\tilde f_ib=b'$ (by (vi) this is equivalent to $b=\tilde e_ib'$). The **crystal of $M$** is this graph, together with the weight function $b\mapsto\mu$ for $b\in B_\mu$. For every $\mu\in P$ one has $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}M_\mu=\operatorname{rank}_{A_0}L_\mu=\#B_\mu$: the first equality holds because $L\otimes_{A_0}\mathbb Q(q)\cong M$ respects the weight decomposition by (ii), and the second because $B_\mu$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $L_\mu/qL_\mu$.

A **crystal basis of the negative half** $U_q^-$ is defined by the same data with $U_q^-$ in place of $M$: a free $A_0$-submodule $L\subseteq U_q^-$ with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}L$ and $\tilde e_iL,\tilde f_iL\subseteq L$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), together with a $\mathbb Q$-basis $B$ of $L/qL$ satisfying (v) and (vi) for the operators on the negative half. Here the root grading replaces the weight grading, and the lattice and residue basis are required to respect that root grading. In the negative half, ẽ_i f̃_i=id implies f̃_iB⊂B; this refinement is specific to its infinite strings. No choice principle is used in these definitions.

For U^-, require the same graded axioms using the negative-half operators; ẽ_i f̃_i=id there shows no nonzero residue basis element is killed by f̃_i. The scalar-extension and rank/residue-count statements follow componentwise from a free lattice and its residue basis. No inference from a finite module endpoint to an infinite negative-half identity is used.

The negative-half reversal star permutes B(infinity) without signs; this unsigned conclusion is proved from the existing signed lattice theorem and positive highest-weight tensor residues, not assumed. The survivors of pi_lambda are exactly c_i(b)<=lambda_i for all i; with weight lambda+wt(b), inherited raising and surviving lowering, and epsilon/phi, they are B(lambda). Any two lowering-generated, everywhere-lowerable negative crystals with strict nonpositive elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum vertex are uniquely isomorphic by their lowering words; the proof uses finite color cycles and terminates after a height bound. Consequently for any field and any general homogeneous nondegenerate Q of the first two lemmas, the shift-orbit simple-module crystal is canonically B(infinity), its first-strand cyclotomic simple graph is B(lambda), and the graph labeled by indecomposable projective COVERS P(S) is the same graph under the unscaled cover–simple pairing.
