scaffold.strategy:
(1) E injects into the rational residue by the hypothesis, hence is Z-torsionfree. Residue surjectivity gives M∩L0⊂Σ_(k=0)^n q^k E+M∩q^(n+1)L0 for every n, by repeatedly subtracting a lift and dividing by q (which preserves M). For x also in q^nL∞, the subtracted terms k≤n lie there; the remainder is in q^n(M∩qL0∩L∞)=0 by residue injectivity on E. Thus M∩L0∩q^nL∞=⊕_(k=0)^n q^kE. Every element of M∩L0 has a finite infinity-pole bound, so the union over n gives Z[q]E. Distinct powers are independent: in a finite relation normalize the lowest exponent and reduce modulo q, then successively remove it. Also M=Z[q±](M∩L0) by finite zero-pole bounds. The analogous infinity-pole argument gives Z[q^-1]E and the mirror residue isomorphism. Since M spans V, Q(q)E spans V; rational residue injection shows a Q-basis of QE is independent and full. Expanding in that basis, zero/infinity valuation gives the full chart extension identities. Freeness over A is claimed only if E is actually finite free over Z.
(2) Laurent expansions in phi(F) have unique finite coefficients: reduce the lowest exponent at0 using the first injection. If an expansion lies in L0 it has no negative exponent; if it lies in L∞ it has no positive exponent, by the second injection. Therefore the intersection is exactly phi(F), with the claimed residue map and factorization. This is finite Laurent linear algebra, not passage to an unjustified formal limit.
(3) Work first on each finitely generated submodule F′ of F; its rational residue injection implies Z-torsionfreeness and hence finite Z-freeness. The balanced factorization of N gives N=(N∩L0)+(N∩L∞). If x∈M∩(L0+N)∩(L∞+N), subtract an element of N to put it in L0. Its remaining discrepancy from L∞ lies in N; split that discrepancy into its zero and infinity chart parts, then subtract its zero chart part to obtain an element of M∩L0∩L∞. Thus the lifts of a finite Z-basis of F′ can be changed by N so that they lie in the simultaneous intersection. Their direct sum with E_N injects into each rational residue: in the quotient modulo QN the F′ component is forced0 by the assumed injection, and then E_N injectivity forces the remaining component0. When F and E_N are finite free, the direct sum description gives E_M finite free. This reproduces the printed diagrams and avoids the native unsupported chart containment, wrong q^nL0/q^nL∞ recursion and coherent-sheaf freeness shortcut.

scaffold.statement: Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient. For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$, $B\otimes_A P(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom duality commutes with this basechange, and finite vector duality commutes with inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels $h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and $T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_B S)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise is used.
scaffold.strategy:
Tensor a shifted-free retract to prove finite projectivity. Every degree-zero endomorphism of $B\otimes P$ lifts through $P\to B\otimes P$ by generic projectivity; endomorphisms preserve $JP$, so this is a surjective endomorphism-ring homomorphism. Its domain is local for indecomposable $P$, hence a nonzero quotient is indecomposable. If $JS=0$, the old cover factors through $P/JP$ and remains essential: pull back a submodule and use the old superfluous kernel. If $JS\ne0$ and $P/JP\ne0$, finite dimension supplies a simple quotient, which must be the old unique head $S$, contradicting its being annihilated by $J$. Every $B$-simple inflates to a generic simple; its descended cover therefore exhausts the projective basis, proving surjectivity and no merging.
For finite $P$, evaluation on a shifted-free module and restriction to retracts gives $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B\otimes P,B)=\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,A)\otimes_A B$. Applying $\psi$ gives $(B\otimes P)^\#=B\otimes P^\#$. Inflation does not change $D_\psi S$. Use only the choice-free finite-module normalization clauses of the generic positive-divided-string supplier. They yield the unique self-dual representatives; no conditional quantum-global clause is used.
Finally $h(P,S)=T(P^\#,S)$ by finite-projective evaluation and $D(P^\psi\otimes S)=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,D_\psi S)$ by evaluation of a tensor functional. A normalized cover has $h(P,S)=q^a$ because absolute $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$. Both dualities fix the normalized labels, so $q^a=q^{-a}$ and $a=0$. Other simple heads have zero Hom. Shift-orbit bases now make both normalized pairings perfect. This proof distinguishes projective Hom duality from vector duality and never uses a symmetric trace.

Write the resulting word as i_1^{r_1}...i_s^{r_s}, adjacent colors distinct. Restriction to a word idempotent is exact. Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable weight module $M$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]], let $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P$ and $u\in L_\lambda$, and let $u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n$ be the admissible $i$-string decomposition of $u$: the sum is finite, $u_n\in\ker E_i\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$, and $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle h_i,\lambda+n\alpha_i\rangle$ ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]). Then:

(a) **Components lie in the lattice.** $u_n\in L\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ for every $n$.

(b) **Lattice string decomposition.** $L_\lambda=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\tilde f_i^{\,n}\bigl(L_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}\cap\ker E_i\bigr)$, the sum being direct because admissible decompositions are unique; equivalently $L=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\tilde f_i^{\,n}(L\cap\ker E_i)$.

(c) **Single surviving component.** If $u+qL=0$ in $L_\lambda/qL_\lambda$, then $u_n\in qL$ for every $n$. If $u+qL\in B_\lambda$, then there is exactly one index $n_0$ with $u_{n_0}\notin qL$, and for it $u_{n_0}+qL\in B_{\lambda+n_0\alpha_i}$, $u\equiv F_i^{(n_0)}u_{n_0}\pmod{qL}$ and $u_{n_0}+qL=\tilde e_i^{\,n_0}(u+qL)$; in particular $n_0=\varepsilon_i(u+qL)$ ([[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]), and $\tilde e_iu$ and $\tilde f_iu$ are the residues of $F_i^{(n_0-1)}u_{n_0}$ and $F_i^{(n_0+1)}u_{n_0}$.

Everything is a statement about the fixed lattice $L$ and the operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$; no finite-dimensionality, bounded support, uniform nilpotence or choice principle is assumed. Here F_i^(−1)u is interpreted as0, and F_i^(a+1)u=0 for a top of coroot weight a, so the final formulas include both finite-string endpoints.
scaffold.strategy:
Tail sums and the partial-inverse axiom, following Kashiwara's Proposition 2.3.2(ii) with JKK Lemma 4.5(a) and Theorem 4.7(b).

(a) Put $T_n:=\tilde e_i^{\,n}u\in L_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ for $n\ge0$: legitimate because $\tilde e_iL\subseteq L$ is axiom (iii) of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]. Since $\tilde e_i$ acts on the string decomposition by $F_i^{(n)}\mapsto F_i^{(n-1)}$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]), $T_n=\sum_{k\ge n}F_i^{(k-n)}u_k$ and hence $\tilde f_iT_{n+1}=T_n-u_n$. As $T_n,T_{n+1}\in L$ and $\tilde f_iL\subseteq L$, each $u_n=T_n-\tilde f_iT_{n+1}$ lies in $L$; the weights are those of the string decomposition.

(b) For $u_n\in L\cap\ker E_i$ the string with top $u_n$ satisfies $\tilde f_i^{\,n}u_n=F_i^{(n)}u_n$, so (a) rewrites $u=\sum_n\tilde f_i^{\,n}u_n$ with every $u_n\in L\cap\ker E_i$; conversely every $\tilde f_i^{\,n}(L\cap\ker E_i)$ lies in $L$ by iterated stability. For a relation among the image summands first discard top components of coroot weight a<n, whose nth image is0; the remaining representatives v_n are admissible. A relation $\sum_n\tilde f_i^{\,n}v_n=0$ is then an admissible decomposition of $0$, so all these representatives v_n=0 by the uniqueness half of [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]; the sum is direct.

(c) Induction on the largest index $N$ of a nonzero string component, proving both clauses simultaneously. The zero vector is immediate. If N=0, u=u0 is a top vector and its residue is either0 or the given basis element, proving both assertions. Let $w:=\tilde e_iu=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n\in L$, whose largest possible string index is N−1, with components u1,…,uN; thus the induction strictly decreases even if u0=0. If $u+qL=0$ then $w+qL=0$; by the induction hypothesis applied to $w$ all of $u_1,\dots,u_N$ lie in $qL$, and then $u_0=u-\tilde f_iw\in qL$ as well, because $u\in qL$ and $\tilde f_iw=\sum_{n\ge1}\tilde f_i^{\,n}u_n\in qL$ (each $\tilde f_i^{\,n}$ preserves $L$, hence maps $qL$ into $qL$). Now let $u+qL=b\in B_\lambda$; then $w+qL=\tilde e_ib\in B\cup\{0\}$ by axiom (v). If $w+qL=0$, the first clause applied to $w$ gives $u_1,\dots,u_N\in qL$, so $u\equiv u_0\pmod{qL}$ and $u_0+qL=u+qL=b\in B$: the claim with $n_0=0$. If $w+qL\in B$, the induction hypothesis applied to $w$ gives a unique index $n_0\ge1$ with $u_{n_0}\notin qL$, $u_{n_0}+qL\in B$ and $w\equiv F_i^{(n_0-1)}u_{n_0}\pmod{qL}$. Applying the linear operator $\tilde f_i$ (which preserves $L$) gives $\tilde f_iw\equiv F_i^{(n_0)}u_{n_0}\pmod{qL}$. On the other hand $u=u_0+\tilde f_iw$, and $(\tilde f_iw)+qL=\tilde f_i(w+qL)=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib=b$ by the partial-inverse axiom, so $\tilde f_iw\equiv u\pmod{qL}$; hence $u_0\equiv0\pmod{qL}$, that is $u_0\in qL$, and $u\equiv F_i^{(n_0)}u_{n_0}\pmod{qL}$ with $u_{n_0}+qL=\tilde e_i^{n_0}b\in B$. Uniqueness of $n_0$ follows from $\tilde e_i^{n}b\ne0$ exactly for $n\le\varepsilon_i(b)$ ([[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]). The final clause is the definition of $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on the string. Every step involves only finite string data and the stability of $L$; no choice principle occurs.

scaffold.statement:
Let $B$ be the crystal of a crystal basis $(L,B)$ of an integrable module ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]], [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]); its operators are the partial maps $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i:B\to B\cup\{0\}$ satisfying $\tilde e_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde f_ib'$, and $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ satisfy $\varphi_i(b)-\varepsilon_i(b)=\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle$.

Define the **dual crystal** $B^\vee:=\{b^\vee:b\in B\}$ by
$$wt(b^\vee):=-wt(b),\qquad \varepsilon_i(b^\vee):=\varphi_i(b),\qquad \varphi_i(b^\vee):=\varepsilon_i(b),\qquad \tilde f_i(b^\vee):=(\tilde e_ib)^\vee,\qquad \tilde e_i(b^\vee):=(\tilde f_ib)^\vee,$$
with $0^\vee:=0$. Then:

(i) $B^\vee$ satisfies the crystal axioms: $(\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i)$ are partial inverses, the arrows of $B^\vee$ are the arrows of $B$ with orientation reversed, the displayed $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ are exactly the maximal iterated powers, and $(B^\vee)^\vee=B$ canonically;

(ii) **tensor products reverse order.** For crystals $B_1,B_2$ as above the map $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto b_2^\vee\otimes b_1^\vee$ is an isomorphism of crystals $(B_1\otimes B_2)^\vee\to B_2^\vee\otimes B_1^\vee$ for the tensor product of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]].

The construction is stated for crystals of crystal bases of integrable modules, where $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ are finite and nonnegative. For the negative-half crystal of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]] only the formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,wt\rangle$, which may be negative, is defined, and no dual is asserted there. No choice principle is used.
scaffold.strategy:
A finite verification from the axioms.

(i) Partial inverses: $\tilde f_i(b^\vee)=b'^\vee$ iff $\tilde e_ib=b'$ iff $b=\tilde f_ib'$ iff $b^\vee=\tilde e_i(b'^\vee)$, which is exactly the required equivalence. Arrows: $b\to b'$ in $B$ means $\tilde f_ib=b'$, and in $B^\vee$ one has $\tilde f_i(b'^\vee)=(\tilde e_ib')^\vee=b^\vee$, so the arrow runs from $b'^\vee$ to $b^\vee$; the orientation is reversed. Maximal iterated powers: $\max\{n:\tilde e_i^n(b^\vee)\ne0\}=\max\{n:\tilde f_i^nb\ne0\}=\varphi_i(b)$ and $\max\{n:\tilde f_i^n(b^\vee)\ne0\}=\varepsilon_i(b)$. Weight pairing: $\varphi_i(b^\vee)-\varepsilon_i(b^\vee)=\varepsilon_i(b)-\varphi_i(b)=-\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle=\langle h_i,wt(b^\vee)\rangle$. Involutivity is immediate from the definition.

(ii) Let S((b1⊗b2)^vee)=b2^vee⊗b1^vee. Set p=phi_i(b1), s=epsilon_i(b2). The f operator on the dual input corresponds to e on b1⊗b2. If p≥s, e acts on b1 and its image under S is b2^vee⊗(e_i b1)^vee=b2^vee⊗f_i(b1^vee). On the target the f rule selects its second factor precisely because phi_i(b2^vee)=s≤p=epsilon_i(b1^vee). If p<s, e acts on b2 and S gives f_i(b2^vee)⊗b1^vee; the target f rule selects its first factor because s>p. The e calculation corresponds to original f: p>s gives the target second factor since s<p, and p≤s gives the target first since s≥p. Zero endpoints agree. The target weight is −wt(b1)−wt(b2), the weight of the dual input; the maximal string lengths therefore agree. This proves the crystal isomorphism with exactly the required tie cases.

scaffold.statement: The theorem of this page is the *degenerate* Ariki categorification theorem: it concerns the tower $H^\Lambda$ over $\mathbb C$ built from the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebras at an integral multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$, and it identifies the two Grothendieck groups at parameter one with the type-$A$ Fock/highest weight data of $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]. It neither states nor implies the categorification theorem for the nondegenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebras $H^\Lambda_{\xi,d}$ at a Hecke parameter $\xi$: the only bridge recorded here is [BK4, Corollary 2], the isomorphism $H^\Lambda_d\cong H^\Lambda_{\xi,d}$ for $\xi$ *not* a root of unity (generic $\xi$), which is not available at roots of unity; at a root of unity of order $e$ the nondegenerate theory is a different theorem, stated for the affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$ Fock space with residues modulo $e$ and graded (canonical-basis) coefficients, supplied by the cyclotomic KLR algebras and the Hecke-KLR isomorphism (the QG-8 track), not by this page. In particular no coefficient computed here determines the root-of-unity graded decomposition data, and the congruence $H^\Lambda_d\cong H^\Lambda_{\xi,d}$ at generic $\xi$ must not be specialized. The generic parameter dictionary is (T_r−xi)(T_r+1)=0 with cyclotomic roots Q_j=xi^m_j on the nondegenerate side, and roots m_j on the degenerate side. The algebra isomorphism is not literal equality of x_r and X_r. The claimed failure is of universal root-parameter transport; particular accidental root-parameter isomorphisms do not supply it. A finite-I theorem concerns its supported central cuts, not an unqualified whole-degree equality.

scaffold.statement:
**Assume the axiom of choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module that is integrable, has finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and weight set contained in a finite union of cones $\lambda-Q_+$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]).

(i) **Splitting along the top isotypic part.** Let $\lambda$ be a maximal weight of $M$, put $N_0:=U_q(\mathfrak g)M_\lambda$ and let $N_1$ be the sum of the remaining simple constituents, so that $M=N_0\oplus N_1$ and $N_0\cong V(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ with $m=\dim M_\lambda$. Then $L=(L\cap N_0)\oplus(L\cap N_1)$, $B=\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_0)/q(L\cap N_0)\bigr)\sqcup\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_1)/q(L\cap N_1)\bigr)$, and both pairs are crystal bases of $N_0$ and $N_1$.

(ii) **Uniqueness.** There is a locally weight-finite indexed family $(\lambda_j)_{j\in J}$ in $P^+$ and an isomorphism of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules $\Phi:M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigoplus_{j\in J}V(\lambda_j)$ with $\Phi(L)=\bigoplus_j\mathcal L(\lambda_j)$ and $\Phi$ inducing a bijection $B\to\bigsqcup_j\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$ of crystals. The multiset $\{\lambda_j:j\in J\}$ is the multiset of highest weights of the simple integrable constituents of $M$: the number of $j$ with $\lambda_j=\lambda$ equals the multiplicity $[M:V(\lambda)]$.

(iii) **Components.** Through $\Phi$ the connected components of the crystal $B$ are exactly the canonical highest weight crystals $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$; each component has a unique highest weight element $b$, of dominant weight $\lambda$, and equals the lowering-generated subcrystal $F(b)$ of [[def-highest-weight-element-and-connected-highest-weight-crystal]]. In particular the crystal graph of any crystal basis of $M$ is determined up to isomorphism by $M$, and no other highest weight elements occur.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared in [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and used to obtain the decomposition of $M$ into simple integrable highest weight modules from [[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], which selects bases of the finite-dimensional maximal-vector spaces simultaneously. It also permits simultaneous choices of lifts of the finite residue bases in the possibly infinite family of top spaces. After those choices, each lattice and crystal argument is finite and choice-free. No incompatible-axiom branch is used, and no global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness is assumed. The index set J need not be finite in affine or indefinite type; local weight finiteness means only finitely many summands contribute to any fixed label-weight space.
scaffold.strategy:
Kashiwara's proof of Theorem 3 in §2.6, transported to the library's conventions, with [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]](iii) playing the role of his Lemma 2.6.1(i).

Step A (structure of the top isotypic part). Each nonzero $w\in M_\lambda$ generates a nonzero integrable cyclic highest weight module of weight $\lambda$, which is $V(\lambda)$ by the universality in [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]; the sum $N_0=U_qM_\lambda$ of these submodules is the $V(\lambda)$-isotypic component, hence $N_0\cong V(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ with $m=\dim M_\lambda$, and $N_1$, the sum of the other isotypic components, is a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-submodule with $M=N_0\oplus N_1$ and no weight $\lambda$ (if lambda is a weight of V(nu), then nu≥lambda is a nonzero weight of M, so maximality of lambda forces nu=lambda).

Step B (descent for $V(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$). Choose lifts in L_lambda of the finite residue basis B_lambda. Their determinant is a q0 unit, so they are an A0-basis; send each lift to the top vector in its own V(lambda) copy. This fixes the top residue basis, not merely the top lattice. Claim: if $u\in V(\lambda)^{\oplus m}_\mu$ with $\mu\ne\lambda$ and $\tilde e_iu\in\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ for all $i$, then $u\in\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$. Take the minimal $n\ge0$ with $q^nu\in\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$; if $n>0$ then $b:=q^nu+q\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}\ne0$ is homogeneous of weight $\mu$ and killed by every $\tilde e_i$, since $\tilde e_i(q^nu)=q^n\tilde e_iu\in q^n\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}\subseteq q\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$. Writing $b=\sum_jb^{(j)}$ componentwise, each $b^{(j)}$ is killed by every $\tilde e_i$, so each $b^{(j)}=0$ by [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]](iii) (note $\mu\ne\lambda$); hence $b=0$, a contradiction.

Step C ($L\cap N_0$ is standard). $L_0:=L\cap N_0$ is a crystal lattice of $N_0$: it is weight-graded, stable under $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$, and generates N0 because its top lattice L_lambda spans M_lambda and lowering words generate U_q M_lambda. Hence $\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}\subseteq L_0$ (it is generated by the $\tilde f_i$-words applied to $(L_0)_\lambda$), and $L_0\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ by descending induction on $\operatorname{ht}(\lambda-\mu)$: for $u\in(L_0)_\mu$ with $\mu\ne\lambda$ every $\tilde e_iu\in(L_0)_{\mu+\alpha_i}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ by induction, so Step B applies, while at $\mu=\lambda$ we have equality of top parts by construction. Thus $L_0=\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$.

Step D (splitting). Weights mu outside lambda−Q_+ have zero N0 component and split trivially; within that cone the following finite-height induction applies. For $u\in L_\mu$ write $u=u_0+u_1$ with $u_j\in N_j$. Descending induction on $\operatorname{ht}(\lambda-\mu)$: at $\mu=\lambda$ we have $u_1=0$ because $N_1$ has no weight $\lambda$; for $\mu\ne\lambda$, $\tilde e_iu\in L_{\mu+\alpha_i}$ has smaller height, so by induction its $N_0$-component $\tilde e_iu_0$ lies in $L_0=\mathcal L(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ (the operators preserve each $N_j$), and Step B gives $u_0\in L_0$; then $u_1=u-u_0\in L\cap N_1$. This proves $L=(L\cap N_0)\oplus(L\cap N_1)$; note that no descent statement for $N_1$ is needed. The two summands are crystal lattices of $N_0,N_1$.

Step E (the residue basis splits). $B_0:=B\cap(L_0/qL_0)$ is linearly independent and stable under $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ by stability of $L_0$, weight-graded, and contains the $m$ top residues; Step F below identifies it with the standard residue basis up to scalars and thereby shows that it spans $L_0/qL_0$. In the remaining part of this step only $B_0\subseteq B$ is used. For $b\in B\setminus B_0$, write $b=b_0+b_1$ in $L/qL=L_0/qL_0\oplus L_1/qL_1$ and suppose $b_0\ne0$; then either $\mu\ne\lambda$ and some $\tilde e_i$ survives on $b_0$ by [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]](iii), so $\tilde e_ib\ne0$ and, by descending induction on the height, $\tilde e_ib\in B_0$ (its $N_1$-component vanishes), whence $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib\in L_0/qL_0\cap B=B_0$ by the partial-inverse axiom, a contradiction; or $\mu=\lambda$ and $b_0\ne0$ is a combination of top residues, so $b\in B_\lambda=B_{0,\lambda}$ because $\#B_\lambda=\dim M_\lambda=m=\#B_{0,\lambda}$. Hence $B=B_0\sqcup B_1$ with $B_1:=B\setminus B_0\subseteq L_1/qL_1$, and counting dimensions weight by weight shows that $B_1$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $L_1/qL_1$.

Step F (identification up to scalars). B0 is the stable subset of B containing all chosen top residues. Step C and the field U-isomorphism identify each chosen top with the top of its own canonical copy. Lowering-word generation identifies B0 with the full standard residue basis and therefore proves it spans and is a crystal basis; no spanning premise is assumed here. In particular its residue basis has exactly one element in each top weight space of the m copies; writing it as $\alpha_j\,b_\lambda^{(j)}$ in the $j$-th copy and using that every vertex of $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is a lowering word from $b_\lambda$ ([[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]](ii)), induction along lowering words shows $B_0=\bigsqcup_j\alpha_j\,\mathcal B(\lambda)^{(j)}$; the scalars are removed by composing the identification with the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-automorphism of $V(\lambda)$ multiplying the highest vector by $\alpha_j^{-1}$ (the top weight space is one dimensional, so this is an automorphism).

Step G (locally finite iteration). Do not assert there are finitely many simple constituents: in affine type, dominant labels lambda−n delta can occur for arbitrarily large n. For any fixed label mu, the set of possible nonzero weights nu≥mu is finite: support lies in finitely many cones lambda_a−Q_+, and nu=mu+gamma=lambda_a−beta requires gamma+beta=lambda_a−mu, whose nonnegative simple-root coefficients give finitely many possibilities. This uses the chosen grading and independent simple roots. Thus one can peel maximal top isotypic components in increasing distance from the finite upper cone bounds; there are finitely many tops at each height and finite multiplicity at each top. Each fixed weight is exhausted after finitely many such removals, so the successive split lattices and residue bases define actual direct sums, not infinite completed sums or a limiting lattice. Equivalently apply the initial semisimple decomposition and the top-splitting lemma locally in that finite upper interval. The projections and identifications are compatible as the interval enlarges because an isotypic component and its standard lattice are fixed after it is split. Choose the top basis lifts in each component as in Step B; any simultaneous choice needed is covered by the declared axiom of choice. This yields Phi, equality of lattices and crystal bases for a possibly infinite locally weight-finite J. Clause(iii) follows componentwise from the canonical highest crystal theorem. No global Laurent freeness or integral splitting is used.

Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with crystal bases $(L_1,B_1)$, $(L_2,B_2)$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ be the integrable module of [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]].

Then $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$, and its crystal is the tensor product crystal $B_1\otimes B_2$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]: for all $b_1\in B_1$, $b_2\in B_2$ and $i\in I$,
$$\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}$$
with value $0$ as soon as the selected factor maps to $0$. In particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ map $B_1\otimes B_2$ into $(B_1\otimes B_2)\cup\{0\}$, and for all $b,b'\in B_1\otimes B_2$ one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$, so the partial-inverse axiom holds. The equality case $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is resolved as in the definition: $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second factor and $\tilde e_i$ on the first.

**Assume the axiom of choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited through [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]]. Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and weight sets contained in finite unions of cones, let $(L_1,B_1),(L_2,B_2)$ be crystal bases of $M_1,M_2$, and let $B_1\otimes B_2$ be the crystal of $M_1\otimes M_2$ ([[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]]).

(a) **Highest vertices.** For $b=b_1\otimes b_2\in B_1\otimes B_2$ the following are equivalent: (i) $b$ is a highest weight element, i.e. $\tilde e_ib=0$ for every $i\in I$; (ii) $\varepsilon_i(b_1)=0$ and $\varepsilon_i(b_2)\le\langle h_i,wt(b_1)\rangle$ for every $i\in I$; (iii) $\varepsilon_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=0$ for every $i\in I$. In this case $wt(b)=wt(b_1)+wt(b_2)$ is dominant.

(b) **Generated components.** For every highest vertex $b\in B_1\otimes B_2$ of weight $\lambda$, the lowering-generated subcrystal $F(b)$ is a connected component of $B_1\otimes B_2$, is isomorphic as a crystal to the canonical $B(\lambda)=\mathcal B(\lambda)$ of [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]], and $\lambda\in P^+$.

(c) **Decomposition.** $B_1\otimes B_2$ is the disjoint union of the subcrystals $F(b)$ over the highest weight elements $b\in B_1\otimes B_2$, each of which is a highest weight crystal in the sense of [[def-highest-weight-element-and-connected-highest-weight-crystal]]; the multiplicity of $B(\lambda)$ as a component equals the multiplicity of $V(\lambda)$ in the tensor product module $M_1\otimes M_2$.

No choice principle beyond the inherited one is used.
scaffold.strategy:

Dominance: $\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle=\varphi_i(b)\ge0$ because $\varepsilon_i(b)=0$ and $\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle$ is finite and nonnegative for a crystal of an integrable module ([[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]).

(b) Apply [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]] to $M_1\otimes M_2$, which satisfies the category hypotheses by [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]](a)-(c), with the crystal basis $(L_1\otimes L_2,B_1\otimes B_2)$ of [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]]. The component of $b$ therefore is a highest weight crystal of weight $\lambda=wt(b)$; by [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]](ii) its vertex set is $F(b)$, and its identification with $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is the transported isomorphism of the uniqueness theorem.

(c) The disjoint-union statement is the component decomposition of the same theorem together with the uniqueness of the highest vertex in each component; the multiplicity statement is clause (ii) there applied to $M_1\otimes M_2$, whose highest weight multiplicities are those of the tensor product module. The axiom of choice is used only through the uniqueness theorem, where it is already declared; no new nonconstructive step occurs.

**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP) $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written $\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]].

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$ is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]), and $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks ([[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the same $e$ and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series ([[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]); a different series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus $\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter, equal to the source's $\xi$) and $q$ (the grading variable, equal to the source's quantum variable) are INDEPENDENT data; the design's phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of a square $q_{\rm src}^2$, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model $\mathcal F_{\rm sym}$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge $0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$, basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$, empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary Dipper–James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Define $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is $\theta$-pullback of $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative Jucys–Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block. At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem [[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]] identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains outside the present nondegenerate regime.

No choice principle is used.
scaffold.strategy: Direct convention check. At level one $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; the finite-characteristic hypothesis $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ makes $\xi\ne1$ a primitive $e$-th root, and in sub-branch (CP) the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ is exactly what makes a primitive $e$-th root exist in $F$. The type-$A$ datum and the grading are batch-24 clauses; the transport statement is the graded block isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. Its Laurent-unit form factor preserves radicals, including zero quotients, and gives $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}\cong(D_{\rm M}^{\lambda})^{\theta}$; apply the involution again. Right-to-left conversion sends $h\cdot m=m h^*$, and commutation $\theta *=*\theta$ preserves the same pullback dictionary. The parameter dictionary is the naming clause of [BK 2009 §1 and §4.2] and [Ariki 1996 §1]; it makes no substitution. No choice is used.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$ fix a reduced decomposition $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put $z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov-Lauda presentation of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]. Their Z-span is closed under integer straightening and is torsion-free inside the characteristic-zero algebra. Thus the integer image is a full finite lattice in this Q-algebra, of rank equal to dim_K H_alpha(K), and K tensor this lattice is H_alpha(K). Homogeneity of generators and relations supplies the integer grading. scaffold.statement:
Fix the level-one type-A integer KLR presentation, charge $0$, and finite quantum characteristic $e\in\{2,3,\ldots\}$. Let $K$ be any characteristic-zero field in the specified Hecke regime, let $\lambda$ be the specified partition, and let $S_K(\lambda)$ be the LEFT graded Murphy cell Specht module with its specified initial cyclic generator $z_K$. Then there is a finite-dimensional graded module $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ for the rational KLR algebra, with a specified homogeneous cyclic vector $z_{\mathbb Q}$, and a graded generator-preserving isomorphism $K\otimes_{\mathbb Q} S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)\cong S_K(\lambda)$. The rational module is explicitly presented by the initial weight, dot and horizontal crossing relations, together with one homogeneous rational relation for each Garnir belt. Each of these relations is the unique vector with Garnir coefficient $1$ in the kernel of a finite matrix with integer entries, obtained from crossing operators in the integer row permutation module. It therefore depends only on the integer presentation, not on a choice of $K$ or of a root of unity.

If the specified normalized simple head $D_K(\lambda)$ is nonzero and absolutely simple, this construction, combined with the local cyclic-head descent lemma, defines its initial-generator image line over $\mathbb Q$ up to scalar. The orbit of that image under the finite integer cyclotomic algebra is a lattice of rank $\dim_K D_K(\lambda)$.
scaffold.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] gives the affine KLR PBW basis. Dot slides remove one crossing from correction terms, quadratic moves remove two, and three-term braid corrections remove three. Preferred reduced expressions differ by terms with strictly fewer crossings.

[F2] [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] fixes the integer coefficients and the source BK/BKW crossing convention $\psi=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$. This proof uses that convention directly; it does not identify KMR's reversed-orientation crossing with it.

[F3] [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] supplies the LEFT Murphy cell Specht module's homogeneous standard basis $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_K$ and triangularity: for every tableau $T$, $v_T$ is a combination of standard $v_U$ with $w_U\le w_T$ in strong Bruhat order. Idempotents and grading restrict this expansion to the vector's weight and degree.

[F4] The specified initial vector has weight $i^\lambda$, all dots kill it, and a crossing kills it when its two successive entries occupy the same initial row. These are the initial-generator relations in the reviewed BKW construction, not conditions imposed on an arbitrary vector in a simple.

[F5] [[lem-integer-cyclic-presentation-descends-the-simple-head-generator-line]] proves characteristic-zero radical base change by the regular trace pairing, hence descends a rational cyclic module's normalized simple head and its specified generator image, and proves the lattice rank.

[F6] [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]] gives the finite free integer cyclotomic algebra used in step 5.2. The local PBW straightening used before that quotient is integral: its monic moves have integer coefficients, and independence follows by rational scalar extension of the supplied PBW basis.

## Proof

**Given:** The stated level-one integer presentation, the specified LEFT cell module and its initial generator, and F1–F5. No Axiom of Choice is used.

1.1 Put $\kappa=0$ in the residue formulas below. Work first in the affine content algebra $R_{\mathbb Z}$ before the cyclotomic quotient. For each row of $\lambda$, the successive residue segment has a one-dimensional integral module on which its word idempotent is $1$ and its dots and internal crossings are $0$. The KLR relations hold: successive colours are distinct, their quadratic at zero dots is $0$, and a possible three-strand repeated-endpoint pattern occurs only for $e=2$, where its double-edge braid correction also vanishes at zero dots. Induce the tensor product of these segment modules, and shift its generator $m_0$ to degree $\deg(T_0)$, where $T_0$ is row reading. Denote the result by $M_{\mathbb Z}$. [F2, construct, algebra]

1.2 Let $P$ be the Young row subgroup. Choose reduced expressions compatible with the unique decomposition $w=d p$, with $d$ a minimal representative for $S_d/P$ and $p\in P$, and $\ell(w)=\ell(d)+\ell(p)$. F1 then makes the inducing bimodule free over the row algebra on the minimal-representative words. Tensoring the one-dimensional row modules shows that $M_{\mathbb Z}$ has the integral basis $m_T=\psi_{w_T}m_0$ indexed by all row-strict tableaux $T$. Its cyclic presentation is exactly the initial weight, dot and horizontal-crossing relations. In particular all generator-action matrices on this finite basis have integer entries. Put $M_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes M_{\mathbb Z}$; scalar extension gives $M_K=K\otimes M_{\mathbb Q}$. By F4, there is a surjective graded map $\pi_K:M_K\to S_K(\lambda)$ carrying $m_0$ exactly to $z_K$. [F1, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

1.3 Crossing straightening gives a filtration useful below: a word with at most $N$ crossings applied to $m_0$ is a combination of $m_U$ with $\ell(w_U)\le N$. Move dots right, reduce nonreduced words by quadratic and Coxeter moves, compare reduced words, and split off the right row subgroup as in step 1.2. Positive dot powers kill $m_0$; a nontrivial row factor ends in an internal crossing and also kills $m_0$. Every correction has fewer crossings. In particular if $s_rT$ is row-strict and $\ell(w_{s_rT})=\ell(w_T)+1$, then $\psi_r m_T=m_{s_rT}$ plus terms of strictly smaller crossing length, with leading coefficient exactly $1$. If $s_rT$ is not row-strict, its possible leading term is killed by the right row factor and only shorter terms remain. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 Fix a Garnir node $A=(a,b)$ with $(a+1,b)\in\lambda$. Its belt consists of the row-$a$ suffix $X$ beginning at column $b$ and row-$(a+1)$ prefix $Y$ ending at column $b$. The entries in these nodes in $T_0$ form one consecutive interval $J=\{u,\ldots,v\}$: the suffix ends at the last position of row $a$, immediately followed by the prefix at the beginning of row $a+1$. Let $G_A$ agree with $T_0$ outside the belt and fill $Y$ first, then $X$, increasingly with $J$. It is row-strict and nonstandard. This $G_A$ is the nonstandard belt filling used for the rational-kernel presentation; it is distinct from the maximal STANDARD Garnir tableau in [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]. [construct, algebra]

2.2 Among ALL row-strict tableaux agreeing with $T_0$ outside this belt, $G_A$ is the only nonstandard one. For columns $c<b$, the upper entry is an unchanged number less than $u$, hence less than every changed lower entry. For columns $c>b$, the lower entry, if present, is unchanged and greater than $v$, hence greater than every changed upper entry. Comparisons with the row above or the row below have the same strict bounds, and every other column comparison is unchanged. Thus only column $b$ can fail. It fails precisely when the first upper-belt entry exceeds the last lower-belt entry. Since each of the two rows is increasing, this is equivalent to every upper-belt entry exceeding every lower-belt entry, and hence to the unique filling $G_A$. [step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 On $J$, the residue word $i(G_A)$ is one successive-residue segment. Along $Y$ the residues increase by $1$; its final node $(a+1,b)$ has residue $\kappa+b-a-1$. The first node of $X$, $(a,b)$, has residue $\kappa+b-a$, and the rest again increase by $1$. Consequently $i(G_A)_r\ne i(G_A)_{r+1}$ for every $u\le r<v$, including $e=2$. This distinctness, rather than any braid normalization, is essential. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

2.4 Let $\delta_A=\deg(\psi_{w_{G_A}}e(i^\lambda))+\deg(T_0)$ and let $T_A^{\mathbb Q}$ be the span of those integral basis vectors $m_T$ for which $T$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt, has weight $i(G_A)$, and has homogeneous degree $\delta_A$. It includes $m_{G_A}$. The use of the entire weight-degree slice avoids any brick-classification assumption. Write $T_A^K=K\otimes T_A^{\mathbb Q}$. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct]

2.5 The vector $\pi_K(m_{G_A})$ is a combination of images of standard basis vectors in $T_A^K$. Indeed F3 gives standard $U$ with $w_U\le w_{G_A}$. The permutation $w_{G_A}$ belongs to the parabolic subgroup generated by $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$, since it permutes only $J$. Every Bruhat-smaller permutation belongs to this same subgroup: choose a reduced word for $w_{G_A}$ in these generators, and use the defining subword characterization of strong Bruhat order. Hence $U$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt. Weight idempotents discard different words, and homogeneity discards different degrees, leaving exactly the standard vectors in the slice of step 2.4. By step 2.2, every other vector of the slice is standard; by F3 its image is part of the standard Specht basis and is linearly independent. Therefore $\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$ is precisely one-dimensional, including the case where the image of $m_{G_A}$ is zero. [F3, step 2.2, step 2.4, algebra]

3.1 For every $u\le r<v$, the image $\psi_r T_A^K$ in $M_K$ is spanned by standard row-strict belt tableaux. To see the support assertion, choose reduced words for all belt permutations using only $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$. Straightening a crossing supported in this interval never introduces a crossing outside it; factoring a right row permutation also uses only this interval. Thus every resulting row-strict basis tableau agrees outside the belt. The image has fixed weight $s_r i(G_A)$, which differs from $i(G_A)$ by step 2.3. Its support cannot include the sole nonstandard belt tableau $G_A$. Hence the entire image has standard support by step 2.2, and $\pi_K$ is injective on its span by F3. [F1, F3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 2.4, algebra]

3.2 If $x\in\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$, then $\pi_K(\psi_r x)=\psi_r\pi_K(x)=0$. The injectivity in step 3.1 implies $\psi_r x=0$ in $M_K$ for every inside-belt crossing. Thus this one-dimensional Specht-kernel line lies in $B_A^K:=\bigcap_{r=u}^{v-1}\ker(\psi_r:T_A^K\to M_K)$. [step 2.5, step 3.1, algebra]

3.3 The $m_{G_A}$ coefficient map is injective on $B_A^K$. Suppose a nonzero $x\in B_A^K$ has that coefficient zero. Choose a tableau $T$ with nonzero coefficient in $x$ whose crossing length $N=\ell(w_T)$ is maximal. It is standard by step 2.2. Record membership in $X$ or $Y$ for the successive numbers $u,\ldots,v$ as a binary word. Unless this word is all $Y$ then all $X$, it has an adjacent occurrence $XY$; that excluded word is exactly $G_A$. Choose such an occurrence at $r,r+1$. Swapping them preserves row strictness because they lie in different rows and are consecutive numbers; it increases permutation length by $1$, because $r$ is in the earlier row. Its weight becomes $s_r i(G_A)\ne i(G_A)$, so it cannot be $G_A$ and is also standard by step 2.2. By step 1.3, the coefficient of $m_{s_rT}$ in $\psi_r x$ at length $N+1$ is precisely the nonzero coefficient of $m_T$ in $x$. A lower-length input cannot reach length $N+1$; a different equal-length input has a different possible leading tableau because $s_r$ is injective; and its correction terms have smaller length. Therefore $\psi_r x\ne0$, contradicting $x\in B_A^K$. [step 1.3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.2, algebra]

3.4 Consequently $\dim_K B_A^K\le1$, while step 3.2 gives a nonzero line inside it. Thus $B_A^K=\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$. Define $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ using the same intersection of crossing kernels over $\mathbb Q$. These are kernels of a single finite stacked matrix with integer entries on the explicitly selected integral row-strict bases. Row reduction over $\mathbb Q$ commutes with extension to $K$, so $B_A^K=K\otimes B_A^{\mathbb Q}$. It follows that $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ is one-dimensional and has a unique rational vector $h_A$ with coefficient $1$ on $m_{G_A}$. Its scalar extension is exactly the Specht-kernel vector with that normalization. This is an explicit rational linear-system construction of the relation, not an assumption that a chosen vector belongs to a rational form. [step 1.2, step 3.2, step 3.3, algebra]

4.1 Every other row-strict belt tableau has strictly smaller crossing length than $G_A$. Outside the belt there are no inversions involving belt entries because the belt interval is consecutive in row reading and its values form $J$. Inside, inversions are exactly upper/lower pairs with the upper entry larger. The tableau $G_A$ has all $|X||Y|$ such inversions, whereas every other filling loses at least one. Hence $h_A=m_{G_A}+\sum_{U:\,\ell(w_U)<\ell(w_{G_A})}c_U m_U$ with rational $c_U$, and it is homogeneous of degree $\delta_A$ by its definition in the slice. [step 2.1, step 2.4, step 3.4, algebra]

4.2 Put $S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}=M_{\mathbb Q}/\sum_A R_{\mathbb Q}h_A$. We prove standard spanning locally. For any nonstandard row-strict $T$, choose a vertical inversion at $(a,b),(a+1,b)$. All entries in its upper suffix $X$ exceed all entries in its lower prefix $Y$. Its Garnir factor $G_A$ therefore satisfies $T=wG_A$ with $w=w_Tw_{G_A}^{-1}$ and $\ell(w)=\ell(w_T)-\ell(w_{G_A})$: reordering the contiguous belt's one-line list from $X,Y$ to $Y,X$ removes precisely its $|X||Y|$ cross inversions, while preserving within-part and outside comparisons. Reduced-word straightening and the relation $h_A=0$ replace $m_T$ by words with fewer than $\ell(w_T)$ crossings, by step 4.1. The filtration of step 1.3 expresses these as row-strict vectors of strictly smaller length. Induction proves that standard vectors span the quotient. [F1, step 1.3, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

4.3 Scalar extension of the rational quotient presentation gives $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}=K\otimes S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}$. Every $h_A$ lies in $\ker\pi_K$ by step 3.4, so $\pi_K$ induces a surjection $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}\to S_K(\lambda)$ preserving the generator and grading. The source is spanned by the standard vectors by step 4.2, and their images are the linearly independent standard Specht basis by F3. Hence this map is an isomorphism. In particular the rational module is finite-dimensional, has its standard basis, and its generator maps exactly to $z_K$. [F3, step 3.4, step 4.2, algebra]

5.1 The rational module factors through the cyclotomic quotient. Each specified cyclotomic relation acts as zero after extension to $K$, because the module in step 4.3 is the specified cyclotomic Hecke cell Specht module. The matrix of that action on the rational standard basis has rational entries; faithful field extension forces it to be zero already over $\mathbb Q$. Denote this rational cyclotomic module by $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$, with generator $z_{\mathbb Q}$ the class of $m_0$. This identifies the required rational initial cyclic generator, not merely the unpointed module's isomorphism class. [step 4.3, algebra]

5.2 If an integer cyclic quotient is desired for F5, take the saturated generator annihilator $I_{\mathbb Z}=\{a\in A_{\mathbb Z}:a z_{\mathbb Q}=0\}$ in the finite integer cyclotomic algebra of [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]]. It is a homogeneous left ideal, and $A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z}$ identifies with the integral orbit $A_{\mathbb Z}z_{\mathbb Q}\subset S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$. Its rational span is the entire rational module by cyclicity, so $\mathbb Q\otimes(A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z})\cong S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ with the specified generator. Clearing denominators in each $h_A$ is also possible, but no unsaturated integer quotient or integral Specht-freeness theorem is needed. [step 5.1, algebra]

5.3 Apply F5 to this pointed rational form and the supplied absolutely simple normalized head. Its radical-basechange proof gives a rational normalized head with the image of $z_{\mathbb Q}$; absolute Schur makes every quotient map to the fixed head differ only by a scalar. Its integral-algebra orbit is finitely generated and torsion-free, with rational span that head, so its rank is exactly the head's $K$-dimension. This establishes the precise requested initial-generator line and lattice statement over arbitrary characteristic-zero $K$. No three-brick identity, unproved R-matrix formula, arbitrary-vector rational form, or change of the specified generator enters the argument. [F5, step 5.1, step 5.2, algebra] ∎

In the situation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. both tableaux are standard, $S=s_rT$, and $r$ occupies an earlier row-reading node than $r+1$, as in [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]), then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the Cartan matrix of the regime.
2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition, then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$ in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].
3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and $S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.
scaffold.strategy: 1 is [BKW, Proposition 3.13]: reduce to $r=d-1$ and compare the two expressions for $\deg(T)$ and $\deg(S)$; the difference is $d_B(\mu^A)-d_B(\mu)$ for the nodes $A$ (containing $d$) and $B$ (containing $d-1$), and the four residue cases (equal residues, adjacent single edge, the $e=2$ double edge, and non-adjacent) give exactly $-2,1,2,0=-a_{i_{d-1}i_d}$. 2 is [BKW, Corollary 3.14], obtained from 1 by multiplying the adjacent transpositions of the reduced word and adding the degrees $\deg(\psi_re(i_T))$. 3 is [BKW, Proposition 3.16]: using the tableau-order Lemma 3.9 reduce to a two-row Garnir belt; the exchange condition $i_S=i_{s_rT}$ splits the belt into bricks of size divisible by $e$ plus at most one exceptional brick per row; Lemma 3.15 computes $\operatorname{codeg}(S)$ and $\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ by the congruence classes of $b$ modulo $e$, and the difference is $-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ in each case. All steps are finite residue and brick computations; no choice. For the strict Garnir case retain the maximal standard belt tableau and strict Bruhat lower condition. Reduce to a two-row belt ending at its final node by the agreement-outside-belt lemma. Remove complete horizontal e-bricks using the ABOVE codegree lemma. The lower tableau has residual codegree -1 if b is nonzero modulo e and 0 otherwise. The Garnir tableau has codegree0/1 for e>2, and1/2 for e=2, respectively. Their difference gives degree1/2 in the single/double-edge cases. Equal-color degree in a standard exchange remains -2, from the Cartan diagonal; it is not assigned +2.

Keep the notation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the vectors $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ may a priori depend on the chosen reduced decompositions $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$. Then:

1. For every $\mu$-tableau $T$ one has $v_T=\sum_{S\unlhd T}a_Sz_S$ with $a_T\ne0$ when $T$ is standard; hence the standard vectors form a basis of $S(\mu)$ triangular with respect to the standard basis $\{z_T\}$ of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].
2. If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced decompositions of the same $w_T$, then $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\unlhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$; in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is independent of the choices.
3. For every $r$ the vectors $e(i)v_T$, $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ are homogeneous, with $$e(i)v_T=\delta_{i,i_T}v_T,\qquad \deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T),\qquad \deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T).$$ Hence $S(\mu)$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module with homogeneous basis $\{v_T\}$ and $q$-character $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

No choice beyond the finite selections of reduced decompositions is used; the resulting graded isomorphism class is independent of them by (2).
scaffold.strategy: Follow [BKW, §4.2-4.3]: (1) expand $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu$ in the standard basis using the quadratic relation, the dot-sliding relations and Lemma 4.1 ($y_rz_\mu=0$, $X_rz_\mu=\xi^{i_r}z_\mu$), and use Proposition 4.3 (triangularity of the $z$-basis) to identify the leading coefficient, which is nonzero exactly for standard $T$. (2) By Matsumoto's theorem it suffices to compare two words differing by one braid relation; the quadratic/braid relations express the difference as a combination of shorter words with the stated weight and degree, and induction on length plus (1) gives the claim. (3) Compute $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ by moving the generators through the reduced word using the mixed relations; every occurring vector has weight $i_T$ or $i_{s_rT}$ and the degrees follow from [[prop-shifted-degrees-and-garnir-exchanges-for-standard-tableaux]] (1) and the definition of $\deg(T)$; the codegree identities of [[lem-degree-and-codegree-of-standard-tableaux]] supply the bookkeeping in the terminal/Garnir cases. The $q$-character formula is then immediate from the homogeneous basis, and forgetting the grading gives the ungraded cell module by construction. This is [BKW, Theorem 4.10] restated; the independence statement is its part (i). No choice.

Keep the notation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], let $\mu$ be a partition of $d$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $i\in I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$. Let $A_1,\dots,A_c$ be the removable $i$-nodes of $\mu$ ordered from bottom to top, and let $\mu^{A_m}=\mu\setminus A_m$. Write $E_i:=E_i^{\rm basic}$ for the restriction functor $N\mapsto e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)N$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]] (equivalently the $i$-part of the tower restriction of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]). Then $E_iS(\mu)$ has a filtration $$0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_c=E_iS(\mu)$$ of graded $R^\Lambda_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$-modules with $V_m/V_{m-1}\cong S(\mu^{A_m})\{d_{A_m}(\mu)\}$ for $1\le m\le c$.

Equivalently, the restriction of $S(\mu)$ to the previous rank has the removable-node filtration of [BKW, Theorem 4.11] over ALL removable nodes, and $E_i$ selects the removable-$i$-node part. No choice is used.
scaffold.strategy: By [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] the module $S(\mu)$ has the homogeneous tableau basis $\{v_T\}$ with $v_T\in e(i_T)S(\mu)$, so the idempotent projection $e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)S(\mu)$ is spanned by those $v_T$ whose last letter is $i$, i.e. whose maximal entry $d$ occupies a removable $i$-node. Set $V_m:=\operatorname{span}\{v_T:\ d\text{ lies in }A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_m\}$; each $V_m$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$-submodule because the generators $y_r,\psi_r$ of the previous rank act by the degree-preserving formulas of [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] (3). The ungraded quotient identification $V_m/V_{m-1}\cong S(\mu^{A_m})$ is [AM, Proposition 1.9] as recalled in [BKW, Theorem 4.11]: deleting the maximal entry from a standard tableau with $d$ in $A_m$ gives a standard $\mu^{A_m}$-tableau, and the map $v_T+V_{m-1}\mapsto v_{T_{\le d-1}}$ is an isomorphism of $H^\Lambda_{d-1}$-modules; the grading shift is computed from the degree recursion $\deg(T)=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_{A_m}(\mu)$, which is exactly the shift $d_{A_m}(\mu)$. The passage from the whole restriction to $E_i$ is the idempotent decomposition $\operatorname{Res}=\bigoplus_iE_i$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] and the definition of $E_i$; order the $i$-nodes bottom to top as in the source. This is [BKW, Theorem 4.11] and [BK 2009, Proposition 5.5]; the independent treatment of the (dual) induced filtration is [Hu-Mathas, Main Theorem]. No choice.
